articles.title: Associação de restaurantes processa Keeta por modelo de delivery | G1
articles.standfirst: Associação Nacional de Restaurantes (ANR) pede suspensão da ‘compra intermediada’, em que, segundo a entidade, restaurantes são incluídos no aplicativo sem autorização prévia; Keeta defende a legalidade da prática.
articles.summary: ANR pede suspensão da ‘compra intermediada’, em que, segundo a entidade, restaurantes são incluídos no aplicativo sem autorização prévia; Keeta defende a legalidade da prática.
articles.body:
Motociclista de entrega com mochila da Keeta. — Foto: Adobe Stock

A Associação Nacional de Restaurantes (ANR) entrou com uma ação civil pública contra a Keeta, plataforma de delivery da chinesa Meituan, na Justiça de São Paulo. A entidade contesta o modelo de “compra intermediada” adotado pela empresa no Brasil. ( entenda mais abaixo )

A associação pede a suspensão imediata da prática nos restaurantes que não autorizaram sua inclusão no aplicativo, além da proibição desse modelo de operação no país.

Segundo a ANR, na “compra intermediada”, restaurantes são incluídos no aplicativo da Keeta sem autorização prévia . Quando um cliente faz um pedido, um entregador ou comprador vai ao estabelecimento, compra os produtos no balcão e os leva ao consumidor.

“Quando a Keeta coloca uma operação dessa, o vendedor nem sabe o que está acontecendo na operação dele. Os gestores de restaurantes não sabem que uma venda presencial de balcão, na verdade, seria uma venda para a Keeta”, disse Erik Momo, presidente do conselho da ANR, em entrevista à Reuters.

Segundo a ANR, a compra intermediada pode limitar a liberdade comercial dos restaurantes, gerar concorrência desleal e prejudicar a relação dos estabelecimentos com os clientes.

“Recorrência é algo fundamental para um restaurante sobreviver. O proprietário tem que ter gestão sobre aquilo que está no cardápio, do item que está vendendo, do preço que está praticando, da qualidade da entrega etc. Se eu, como proprietário, passo tudo para esse intermediário e perco esse controle, estou correndo o risco de meu negócio deixar de existir sem eu saber”, disse Momo.

Além de pedir a suspensão da prática, a ANR defende maior diálogo da Keeta com o setor. A entidade cita como exemplo suas parcerias com o iFood, controlado pelo grupo Prosus, e a 99, da chinesa DiDi Global.

“Nosso pedido é que eles suspendam essa prática. Ela é prejudicial para o consumidor, porque ele não entende o que está acontecendo, e para o restaurante, porque ele acaba vendendo algo que não estava previsto”, disse Momo.

Procurada pela Reuters, a Keeta, que iniciou suas operações no Brasil em 2025, afirmou não ter recebido nenhuma notificação judicial sobre a ação.

Sobre a compra intermediada, a empresa afirmou que a ferramenta foi criada em caráter experimental para ampliar as opções de restaurantes disponíveis aos consumidores no aplicativo.

Segundo a Keeta, a iniciativa foi desenvolvida em um mercado no qual contratos de exclusividade dificultam a entrada de estabelecimentos em outras plataformas de delivery.

"A compra intermediada [é] uma iniciativa desenvolvida especificamente para o Brasil e que opera em conformidade com todas as leis e regulamentações locais aplicáveis", disse a Keeta em nota.

A Keeta iniciou suas operações no Brasil em 2025. A 99, da também chinesa DiDi Global, retomou sua atuação no setor de delivery no mesmo ano. Desde então, as duas empresas vêm ampliando suas operações no país, enquanto o iFood segue na liderança do mercado.

Em setembro, o Tribunal do Conselho Administrativo de Defesa Econômica ( Cade ) determinou o aprofundamento das investigações sobre a concorrência no mercado de delivery no Brasil.

articles.title: Dólar opera em alta, com balanços corporativos e pesquisas eleitorais no foco; Ibovespa cai | G1
articles.standfirst: Na véspera, a moeda americana caiu 0,58%, cotada a R$ 5,0188. Já a bolsa brasileira subiu 1,57%, aos 208.296 pontos.
articles.summary: Na véspera, a moeda americana caiu 0,58%, cotada a R$ 5,0188. Já a bolsa brasileira subiu 1,57%, aos 208.296 pontos.
articles.body:
O dólar abriu a sessão desta quarta-feira (21) em alta, com um avanço de 0,12% perto das 10h50, cotado a R$ 5,0246 . Já o Ibovespa , principal índice da bolsa brasileira, tinha queda de 0,24% no mesmo horário, aos 207.802 pontos .

Com as eleições brasileiras como pano de fundo, investidores aguardam pela divulgação de novas pesquisas eleitorais e avaliam novos balanços corporativos. A notícia de que o Banco Central estuda medidas para conter o endividamento das famílias e os preços do petróleo no mercado internacional também seguem no radar.

▶️ A temporada de balanços no Brasil começou nesta semana e deve mexer com os mercados financeiros. Analistas indicam que, principalmente nos resultados do setor financeiro, os índices de inadimplência estarão no centro das atenções, principalmente após o rali presidencial.

▶️ Com isso, investidores também seguem atentos ao cenário de crédito , após notícias de que o Banco Central estaria estudando um conjunto de medidas para conter o endividamento das famílias no Brasil. Entre as medidas, estariam a maior transparência dos bancos, a conscientização do consumidor e o limite do crédito autorizado por pessoa de acordo com a renda.

▶️ Além disso, a nova pesquisa Quaest de intensão de votos também fica no foco. O levantamento mostrou Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) com 45% das intenções de voto, contra 44% de Lula. A situação é de empate técnico, com 1 ponto de diferença entre os dois candidatos. A pesquisa também indicou que 44% temem volta da família Bolsonaro ao poder e 42%, mais um mandato de Lula.

▶️ No exterior, destaque para novos dados sobre estoques semanais de petróleo nos Estados Unidos . O indicador deve trazer novos sinais sobre as condições de oferta e demanda, em meio à volatilidade dos preços da commodity no mercado internacional e diante das tensões ainda elevadas no Oriente Médio.

Perto das 9h, o barril do Brent , referência internacional, subia 0,57% , cotado a US$ 109,41. Já o West Texas Intermediate ( WTI ), referência nos EUA, avançava 0,84% no mesmo horário, a US$ 98,64 o barril. Na véspera, o petróleo teve a maior cotação em cinco meses. Saiba mais.

Veja abaixo mais detalhes do dia no mercado.

As tensões entre os Estados Unidos e o Irã seguem influenciando as cotações do petróleo no mercado internacional. Na véspera, o Teerã informou ao comandante do Exército do Paquistão que não haverá negociações com Washington até que suas exigências sejam atendidas.

As falas reforçam o endurecimento da postura do país em relação às tratativas com os EUA, apesar dos esforços de mediação do Paquistão, seu principal interlocutor.

Segundo o presidente iraniano, Masoud Pezeshkian, Washington não poderá conquistar a confiança de Teerã até que cumpra as sete condições apresentadas pelo país no mês passado para a reabertura do Estreito de Ormuz, rota por onde passava cerca de 20% de todo o comércio global de petróleo antes da guerra.

As condições do Irã incluem, entre outras exigências, o fim do bloqueio dos EUA aos seus portos, o fim das sanções dos EUA às suas exportações de petróleo, bem como o fim das hostilidades em todas as frentes regionais.

As tensões continuam a trazer volatilidade para os preços do petróleo. Na véspera, o barril do Brent chegou a superar os US$ 111, no maior nível em cinco meses.

Desde o início do conflito, no entanto, os países tem buscado rotas alternativas no Golfo Pérsico, em uma tentativa de mitigar o impacto do conflito. Segundo o presidente do grupo HSBC, Georges Elhedery, esse investimento pode até tornar o Estreito de Ormuz "desnecessário" nos próximos cinco anos.

O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), candidatos à Presidência da República, participaram na noite de domingo (18) do primeiro debate do segundo turno das eleições de 2026.

“Acreditamos que essa região será capaz de se recuperar e, em seguida, continuar crescendo. Isso exigirá muitos investimentos”, disse o executivo durante evento do HSBC, em Dubai.

“É claro que desejamos e esperamos ver uma resolução para o conflito... Mas o Estreito de Ormuz, provavelmente daqui a cinco anos, pode se tornar obsoleto”, acrescentou.

Em Wall Street , os três principais índices acionários da região operam em alta nesta quarta-feira, depois que os resultados trimestrais da SpaceX e da Super Micro Computer aumentaram o apetite por ações do setor de inteligência artificial.

Perto das 10h50, o Dow Jones tinha subia 0,20%, enquanto o S&P 500 avançava 0,22% e o Nasdaq Composite tinha ganhos de 0,68%.

O dia também era bastante positivo na Europa, com ações impulsionadas por balanços corporativos. No mesmo horário, o DAX , da Alemanha, tinha alta de 1,42%, enquanto o CAC-40 , da França, subia 0,98% e o FTSE 100 , do Reino Unido, ganhava 0,25%.

Na Ásia , as bolsas fecharam mistas nesta quarta-feira, em meio a esperanças cada vez menores de que o governo chinês faça um grande estímulo para impulsionar gastos. Balanços corporativos também ficaram no radar.

O SSEC , Índice de Xangai, teve queda de 0,6%, enquanto o CSI300 , que reúne grandes empresas chinesas, caiu 1,0%. No Japão, o Nikkei avançou 0,85%, enquanto o Kospi , da Coreia do Sul, valorizou 3,29%. O Hang Seng , de Hong Kong, teve perdas de 0,90%.

articles.title: INSS: Justiça libera R$ 2,9 bilhões em atrasados; veja quem tem direito a receber e como consultar | G1
articles.standfirst: Valor será pago a 193,2 mil beneficiários que venceram ações judiciais contra o INSS; veja como consultar se você está na lista e quando o dinheiro poderá ser sacado.
articles.summary: Valor será pago a 193,2 mil beneficiários que venceram ações judiciais contra o INSS; veja como consultar se você está na lista e quando o dinheiro poderá ser sacado.
articles.body:
A cobrança do INSS era indevida, o que justificou a indenização por danos morais — Foto: Divulgação / INSS

O Conselho da Justiça Federal (CJF) liberou R$ 3,5 bilhões para o pagamento de valores atrasados a pessoas que venceram ações contra órgãos do governo federal.

Do total, R$ 2,9 bilhões são destinados a ações relacionadas ao INSS e a benefícios assistenciais, incluindo casos de revisão de aposentadorias , pensões , auxílio por incapacidade e outros benefícios.

Os recursos atendem 313.181 beneficiários em 243.718 processos no total.

Em número de processos, as ações relacionadas ao INSS e a benefícios assistenciais representam 57% do total de Requisições de Pequeno Valor (RPVs) liberadas e concentram aproximadamente 83% do dinheiro .

São valores que o governo deixou de pagar ou pagou a menos e que, após decisão judicial, precisam ser quitados. Esses valores são chamados de atrasados.

O CJF libera os recursos para os Tribunais Regionais Federais (TRFs), que são responsáveis por fazer os depósitos.

O dinheiro é colocado em uma conta específica, aberta para cada beneficiário no Banco do Brasil ou na Caixa Econômica Federal . Ou seja, o valor não é depositado automaticamente na conta bancária que a pessoa usa normalmente.

Depois que o TRF informar que o pagamento está disponível, o beneficiário pode sacar o dinheiro diretamente em uma agência do banco indicado, apresentando os documentos necessários. Em determinadas situações, também é possível pedir a transferência do valor para uma conta indicada pelo advogado.

A data em que o dinheiro estará apto deve ser consultada no site do TRF responsável pelo processo.

Para receber os atrasados, não basta ter um pedido de aposentadoria ou benefício negado pelo INSS, é preciso ter vencido uma ação judicial contra o órgão e ter uma RPV incluída no lote.

Consulte o andamento do seu processo na Justiça Federal;

Procure informações sobre a expedição da RPV ou sobre a liberação do pagamento;

Consulte o TRF responsável pelo processo. É o TRF que informa quando o dinheiro estará disponível;

Tenha em mãos o número do processo ou do CPF, conforme o sistema de consulta do tribunal.

articles.title: Justiça autoriza recuperação judicial da Casas Bahia | G1
articles.standfirst: Grupo terá 30 dias para entregar documentos pendentes; decisão pode ser revogada se determinação não for cumprida.
articles.summary: Grupo terá 30 dias para entregar documentos pendentes; decisão pode ser revogada se determinação não for cumprida.
articles.body:
Unidade da Casas Bahia. — Foto: Varejo/Divulgação

A Justiça de São Paulo autorizou, nesta quarta-feira (21), o início da recuperação judicial da Casas Bahia e de outras nove empresas do grupo. A decisão foi assinada pela juíza Tainá Maria Leonardo de Oliveira, da 2ª Vara de Falências e Recuperações Judiciais do Foro Central Cível de São Paulo.

Segundo a decisão, as empresas cumprem os requisitos legais necessários para avançar com a recuperação, apesar de ainda haver documentos pendentes.

O grupo terá 30 dias para apresentar as informações que faltam. Caso não cumpra a determinação, a autorização poderá ser revogada. Entre as pendências estão dados sobre o fluxo de caixa de 2023 de quatro empresas, projeções financeiras separadas para cada companhia e a atualização da lista de credores.

A magistrada também manteve a suspensão temporária de determinadas cobranças judiciais contra as empresas, medida que já havia sido concedida anteriormente.

Apesar das pendências, a juíza avaliou que os problemas identificados na documentação são pontuais e podem ser corrigidos durante o processo.

🔎 Nesta fase, a Justiça avalia apenas se as empresas cumprem os requisitos legais e se apresentaram os documentos necessários para iniciar a recuperação judicial. A decisão não significa que o plano de recuperação foi aprovado nem que a Justiça concluiu que as empresas conseguirão se recuperar. O plano ainda precisa passar pela análise dos credores.

A AJ Ruiz Consultoria Empresarial S/A foi nomeada administradora judicial, responsável por acompanhar e fiscalizar as atividades das empresas durante o processo e apresentar relatórios à Justiça.

Após a publicação do edital, os credores terão 15 dias para informar créditos que não estejam na lista ou contestar os valores apresentados pela empresa. Os pedidos deverão ser encaminhados diretamente à administradora judicial.

O Grupo Casas Bahia entrou com o pedido de recuperação judicial em 16 de agosto , om o objetivo de renegociar cerca de R$ 17,3 bilhões em dívidas e manter suas operações.

🔎 A recuperação judicial permite que empresas em dificuldades financeiras tentem renegociar suas dívidas sob supervisão da Justiça enquanto mantêm suas atividades. O mecanismo busca evitar a falência e preservar a operação e os emprego. ( Veja como funciona a recuperação judicial )

articles.title: União Europeia pode liberar importação de frango e mel do Brasil após suspensão | G1
articles.standfirst: Comissão Europeia vai propor que o bloco volte a comprar os produtos brasileiros após auditoria com resultados positivos, mas não prevê, por enquanto, retomar as importações de carne bovina.
articles.summary: Comissão Europeia vai propor que o bloco volte a comprar os produtos brasileiros após auditoria com resultados positivos, mas não prevê, por enquanto, retomar as importações.
articles.body:
A Comissão Europeia afirmou nesta quarta-feira (21) que pretende propor a retomada das importações de carne de aves e mel do Brasil, apurou a agência de notícias Reuters.

A medida ainda precisa ser votada pelos países-membros do bloco, em uma próxima reunião do comitê responsável pelo tema.

🔍 A UE tirou o Brasil da lista de países que cumprem as suas regras sobre o uso de antimicrobianos na pecuária . Essas substâncias são usadas para tratar infecções em animais, mas o bloco proíbe seu uso para estimular o crescimento. Também proíbe o uso, em animais, de antimicrobianos reservados ao tratamento de seres humanos. ( entenda aqui)

O embargo passou a falar no dia 3 de setembro, e incluí também a carne bovina, pescados e ovos para as 27 nações do bloco.

Em nota divulgada nesta quarta, a Comissão Europeia informou que apresentou os resultados de uma auditoria realizada no Brasil sobre a produção de carne de aves e mel. Segundo o órgão, as conclusões foram positivas.

Durante a reunião, os países-membros também tiveram dúvidas sobre o alcance da proposta , os mecanismos para separar produtos destinados a diferentes mercados e os controles das prescrições veterinárias . Esses pontos foram discutidos, segundo a Comissão.

O anúncio da exclusão do Brasil da lista de fornecedores foi feita em maio.

A medida não foi motivada por irregularidades encontradas na carne brasileira, mas pela avaliação da União Europeia de que o controle feito pelo Brasil sobre o uso dessas substâncias é insuficiente.

As carnes bovina e de frango são os produtos mais afetados, pois estão entre os itens de origem animal mais exportados pelo Brasil para a UE. Ainda assim, representam uma parcela pequena do valor total exportado pelo país.

Em 24 de agosto, tiveram início ass auditorias nos setores de aves e mel, feitas por solicitação das próprias autoridades da União Europeia.

Os fiscais visitaram estabelecimentos produtivos e órgãos oficiais do país, verificando a estrutura e do funcionamento do sistema oficial de defesa agropecuária brasileiro.

Segundo a Comissão Europeia, o Brasil ainda não consegue certificar de forma confiável que atende às exigências aplicáveis durante toda a vida dos animais. Por isso, o órgão não pretende, neste momento, propor a retomada das importações desse produto.

A retomada das exportações deste produto tende a ser demorada porque a UE exige que seus fornecedores comprovem que não houve uso de antimicrobianos durante todo o ciclo de vida do animal — que, no caso do boi, leva, em média, dois anos, explica o chefe-adjunto da Delegação da UE no Brasil, Jean-Pierre Bou.

Em junho, na tentativa de reverter a decisão da UE, o governo federal implementou um novo protocolo de controle sobre uso de antimicrobianos na pecuária , que prevê o rastreamento do animal desde o nascimento até o abate.

Para o presidente da Associação Brasileira das Indústrias Exportadoras de Carne (Abiec), Roberto Perosa, é importante que o Brasil volte para a lista da União Europeia, já que ela serve de referência para mais de 20 países fora do bloco, incluindo o Reino Unido e nações africanas.

A Noruega, por exemplo, também interrompeu as compras de proteína animal do Brasil, seguindo a decisão da UE.

Bandeira da União Europeia. — Foto: Christian Lue/Unplash

articles.title: Tesla e SpaceX discutem possível fusão; ‘boa ideia’, diz Musk | G1
articles.standfirst: Negociações começaram nas últimas semanas e podem resultar na compra da Tesla pela SpaceX, segundo fonte ouvida pela Reuters.
articles.summary: Negociações começaram nas últimas semanas e podem resultar na compra da Tesla pela SpaceX, segundo fonte ouvida pela Reuters.
articles.body:
Musk, Spacex e Tesla — Foto: REUTERS/Evan Vucci e REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Ilustração

Elon Musk afirmou, na terça-feira (20), que uma possível fusão entre a SpaceX e a Tesla seria “uma boa ideia” e revelou que as duas empresas criaram comitês especiais para discutir a operação. Após as declarações, as ações da SpaceX subiram 8% nas negociações após o fechamento do mercado.

A SpaceX também divulgou seu primeiro lucro desde que abriu o capital. O bilionário afirmou esperar que a receita recorrente anual da companhia fique entre US$ 500 bilhões (R$ 2,5 trilhões) e US$ 1 trilhão (R$ 5 trilhões) até o fim de 2027, impulsionada pela crescente demanda por capacidade em seus centros de dados com o avanço da inteligência artificial.

🔎 Receita recorrente anual é uma estimativa de quanto uma empresa pode faturar em um ano com receitas que se repetem regularmente.

Musk já havia levantado anteriormente a possibilidade de unir SpaceX e Tesla , citando a crescente sobreposição entre os negócios das duas companhias.

As especulações sobre uma possível compra da fabricante de veículos elétricos pela empresa espacial ganharam força recentemente, depois que o Barclays afirmou, na semana passada, que um acordo poderia ser anunciado antes da assembleia anual da Tesla , em dezembro.

“Acho que seria uma boa ideia, mas isso realmente depende dos comitês especiais das duas empresas”, disse Musk, na primeira confirmação oficial de que SpaceX e Tesla mantêm conversas formais sobre uma possível fusão.

“Como tenho conflito de interesses, não posso participar das discussões dos comitês especiais”, afirmou o bilionário durante uma teleconferência com investidores. Os grupos são formados por conselheiros independentes.

Os comitês especiais foram criados a pedido dos acionistas, que também teriam de aprovar uma eventual fusão.

A Terafab, empresa criada em conjunto por SpaceX e Tesla para fabricar chips, deve produzir seu primeiro chip de teste entre maio e junho de 2027 e pretende iniciar a produção em larga escala até o terceiro trimestre de 2028, segundo Musk.

Musk ressaltou, porém, que ainda é cedo para considerar a fusão como certa. Segundo ele, os comitês especiais ainda não chegaram a um acordo sobre os termos da operação e podem nunca chegar. As ações da Tesla subiam 1,8% nas negociações após o fechamento do mercado.

Musk, a pessoa mais rica do mundo, detém quase 20% da Tesla e pouco menos de 50% da SpaceX . Segundo analistas, uma fusão lhe daria o controle da empresa resultante.

As negociações começaram nas últimas semanas e podem resultar na compra da Tesla pela SpaceX , segundo uma fonte a par das discussões ouvida pela Reuters. A pessoa pediu anonimato por não estar autorizada a falar publicamente sobre o assunto. A Tesla também conta com a assessoria de um banco de investimentos nas negociações.

A receita da SpaceX cresceu 161% no terceiro trimestre, para US$ 14,58 bilhões (R$ 73,1 bilhões), na comparação com o mesmo período do ano anterior. A receita ligada à inteligência artificial aumentou quase dez vezes, para US$ 7,56 bilhões (R$ 37,9 bilhões), impulsionada principalmente pelo aluguel de capacidade de seus centros de dados a empresas como Anthropic, Google , da Alphabet , e Reflection AI, e não por modelos próprios de IA.

Os resultados do terceiro trimestre mostram que os investimentos da SpaceX em inteligência artificial já começam a gerar receita, embora os gastos com infraestrutura de computação continuem elevados. Os investimentos da empresa em ativos e infraestrutura quase triplicaram, para US$ 19,6 bilhões (R$ 98,3 bilhões).

O avanço da inteligência artificial está mudando o perfil dos negócios da SpaceX , historicamente impulsionados pelo serviço de internet via satélite Starlink. As ambições de longo prazo da empresa também dependem do início das operações regulares dos foguetes Starship.

articles.title: Cursos gratuitos de culinária natalina em Sergipe: 140 vagas abertas | G1
articles.standfirst: Os interessados podem se inscrever pela plataforma digital GO Sergipe ou presencialmente na Diretoria de Economia Solidária da Secretaria de Estado do Trabalho, Emprego e Empreendedorismo.
articles.summary: Cursos gratuitos de culinária natalina em Sergipe recebem inscrições pelo portal GO Sergipe ou presencialmente na Seteem para aulas realizadas no Senac Aracaju.
articles.body:
Panetone; chocotone; culinária natalina — Foto: Daniele Melo/Governo de Sergipe

O Programa Qualifica Sergipe está com 140 vagas abertas para cursos gratuitos de culinária natalina, distribuídos em três capacitações: roscas e panetones, comidas natalinas e doces finos para festas.

De acordo com o governo do estado, os cursos têm carga horária de 20 horas e serão realizados na unidade do Serviço Nacional de Aprendizagem Comercial (Senac) localizada na Avenida Ivo do Prado, em Aracaju , nos turnos da tarde e da noite.

As vagas estão distribuídas em sete turmas, e as inscrições ficam abertas até o preenchimento total das vagas.

Os interessados podem se inscrever pela plataforma GO Sergipe ou presencialmente na Diretoria de Economia Solidária da Secretaria de Estado do Trabalho, Emprego e Empreendedorismo (Seteem), localizada na Casa do Trabalhador, no Edifício Maria Feliciana, na Travessa Baltazar Góis, nº 86, no Centro da capital, com acesso pela Rua Itabaianinha. O atendimento presencial ocorre de segunda a sexta-feira, das 8h às 13h.

Para participar dos cursos, é necessário ter no mínimo 18 anos e o 5º ano do Ensino Fundamental concluído.

The pace set a record for the quickest full subscription of a public issue.On the National Stock Exchange, RIL shares advanced as much as 1.96 per cent to Rs 1,225.60 apiece. crude oil, European natural gas and agricultural commodities facing significant upside risks, according to a recent report by Goldman Sachs.The bank said escalating attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, damage to energy infrastructure and the possibility of a colder-than-average European winter could drive energy prices sharply higher.However, its base-case forecast anticipates some moderation as supplies from the Middle East recover and the risk premium eases.“Our base case is that a further recovery in Mideast supply and a moderation in the risk premium reduce prices of Brent crude and European natural gas to $90/bbl and EUR70/MWh, respectively, by end-2026,” the report said.The bank warned that a prolonged disruption to Gulf oil supplies could push prices considerably higher in 2027.“Brent might rally to $140 in early 2027 and average around $125/bbl in 2027” if average Gulf output remains 5 million barrels per day below February 2026 levels, it said.European natural gas prices could also climb to 150 euros per megawatt-hour by the end of 2026 if liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports from the Persian Gulf remain depressed and winter temperatures turn substantially colder than average.Middle East tensions keep oil supply risks in focusOil prices rose on Wednesday as escalating tensions in the Middle East heightened concerns over supply disruptions, while falling US crude and fuel inventories provided additional support to the market, according to Reuters.Brent crude futures climbed $1.61, or 1.5 per cent, to $110.40 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained $1.45, or 1.5 per cent, to $99.27 per barrel as of 0630 GMT.The gains followed a decline in the previous session after Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian discussed mediation efforts with Pakistan's army chief in Tehran. However, uncertainty over a possible diplomatic breakthrough continued to weigh on market sentiment."Oil prices have been having a bit of wild ride in the last couple of sessions," Suvro Sarkar, head of energy research at DBS, told Reuters.He attributed the fluctuations to a combination of profit-taking, hopes of a Qatar- or Pakistan-brokered deal and concerns that any agreement remained distant, alongside continued drawdowns in US crude and petroleum product inventories.Maritime security risks have also intensified. Ship-tracking firm Kpler recorded at least 18 vessel attacks over the preceding two weeks. LSEG analysts warned that attacks on tankers had extended beyond the Strait of Hormuz into the Gulf of Oman, threatening regional oil loadings and ship-to-ship transfers.The Houthis also claimed responsibility for attacks on a Saudi Aramco site in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield and airports in Riyadh and Abha. Meanwhile, the death toll from a Houthi attack on Yemeni government forces rose to 73.Agricultural markets face weather and supply pressuresBeyond energy, Goldman Sachs warned that agricultural commodities faced mounting risks from the Iran and Russia-Ukraine conflicts, potential restrictions on food exports and the prospect of a severe El Niño weather pattern.The bank said the agriculture component of the Bloomberg Commodity Index had risen 19 per cent year-on-year. Disruptions to fertiliser shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and grain exports through the Black Sea could add to costs and tighten supplies.“A strengthening El Niño has a greater than 81% probability of reaching ‘super’ El Niño conditions,” the report said, warning that the weather pattern could disrupt crop production through droughts and floods across key agricultural regions.The outlook comes amid wider concerns about the impact of geopolitical disruptions on global supply chains. articles.body: NEW DELHI: HDFC Bank has found evidence that two senior executives shared confidential business plans and possibly market-sensitive information with outsiders, according to a Bloomberg report.The probe began after some bank leaders raised concerns about possible leaks. articles.title: The era of 'tokenmaxxing' is over — and investors shouldn't take unlimited AI demand for granted
articles.summary: The slowdown in token spending among corporations suggests the appetite for compute only exists at the right price.
articles.body:
The era of tokenmaxxing is officially over. That's because the demand for computing capacity isn't actually unlimited, as AI boosters once touted.

Instead, compute appears to be highly price-sensitive, as buyers facing higher prices and lower returns cut back on usage or pivot to cheap open-source alternatives.

That's the key finding in a new blog post by Apollo chief economist Torsten Sløk: don't take AI demand for granted.

(Disclosure: Yahoo is a portfolio company of funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.)

Ultimately, the key metric that will define the AI build-out isn't physical capacity or power, Sløk said, but the price users are willing to pay for the compute being built. And token spending has sharply decreased.

The slowdown in token spending among corporations suggests that the lavish appetite for compute only exists at the right price — when it is effectively free.

An analysis of declining returns on invested capital for the five largest hyperscalers suggests invested capital grows faster than the earnings it generates. That mismatch gets at the heart of the AI bull case and gives investors questions to ask and numbers to watch for as we get deeper into Big Tech earnings.

Companies are willing to pay a high price for compute, he said, if they are able to boost revenues, squeeze out better profit margins, or cut costs. But such results at a meaningful scale aren't showing up yet.

So far, he said, the AI payoff has been slow to materialize. That suggests more companies are reluctant to dedicate resources to pay for AI services. Those returns may actually emerge. But the uncertainty comes at a price.

Hamza Shaban is a reporter for Yahoo Finance covering markets and the economy. Follow Hamza on X @hshaban .

articles.title: Where people make over $1 million a year but still choose to rent
articles.summary: The number of renters earning $1 million or more more than tripled between 2020 and 2024, a sign that renting by choice is growing more popular.
articles.body:
For even America's highest earners, renting can look more appealing than buying a home.

The number of renters in the US earning $1 million and up more than tripled between 2020 and 2024, according to RentCafe data, outpacing the growth in high-earning homeowners during the same period.

The data suggests that even the country's highest earners , while likely able to afford to buy if they wanted to, aren't immune to trends that have pushed millions of Americans to rent for longer . High mortgage rates still curtail their buying power, strong stock market performance makes tying up money in a home look less appealing, and renting can be a more flexible option than going through the process of buying and selling a high-end home.

Most $1 million-earning renter households are concentrated in the nation's priciest cities, where salaries tend to be higher and the cost differential between renting and owning often aggressively favors renting.

In New York City, home to more than 7,000 of these high-earning renters, a monthly rent of $15,000 to $20,000 — considered "comfortable" on that income by conventional affordability metrics — can cover a two- or three-bedroom apartment overlooking Central Park or a two-story unit in the trendy West Village. Buying a comparable unit, though, usually costs far more after factoring in high mortgage rates, taxes, and monthly maintenance fees.

San Francisco has the second-highest population of high-earning renters, with more than 1,800, followed by Los Angeles with 1,500.

But high-earning renters are increasingly popping up in small and midsize cities. Harrisburg, Pa., the state's capital, now has more than 140 renter households making over $1 million, up from just three in 2020. In Provo, Utah, the figure jumped from 10 to 264 in four years. Des Moines, Iowa, saw its highest-earning renters increase from four to 92 during the same period.

Most high-earning renters work in well-paying industries such as technology and finance or hold executive or managerial roles within their companies. About three-quarters of renter households bring in more than $1 million a year by combining two relatively high salaries, rather than having a single person rake in seven figures.

Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

articles.title: Elon Musk's SpaceX is now mostly an AI company: Chart of the Day
articles.summary: Investors bought SpaceX for the rockets. Instead, they're getting an AI cloud.
articles.body:
Investors bought SpaceX for the rockets. They're getting an AI cloud.

The company's AI segment, freshly renamed "Super Intelligence," brought in $7.6 billion in the third quarter, SpaceX ( SPCX ) reported Tuesday. That's more than Starlink and the rocket business combined, and more than half of SpaceX's $14.6 billion in total revenue.

A year ago, AI made up about 15% of sales. In SpaceX's first report as a public company , it was a third. One quarter later, Starlink lost its top spot.

So what is Super Intelligence, exactly? Mostly a landlord. About $7 billion came from renting out computing power and selling AI software like Grok. Ads on X, the platform Musk bought for $44 billion, chipped in just over half a billion.

The coding startup Cursor, acquired in August, added $608 million. Even without it, Super Intelligence would have topped Starlink, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.

And the AI business is finally making money. It posted its first quarterly operating profit, $431 million, even after absorbing $1.2 billion in Cursor-related stock compensation. By adjusted EBITDA , a profit measure that skips non-cash charges, it out-earned Starlink.

SpaceX credited "a clear inflection in our Super Intelligence business" in its earnings release.

Starlink isn't exactly limping, either. It added 1.6 million consumer subscribers in the quarter.

Of course, becoming an AI company isn't cheap. SpaceX spent $19.6 billion on capital expenditures in the quarter, and 84% of it went to Super Intelligence.

Notice the gap between the bars is shrinking. In the second quarter, SpaceX spent more than twice what it brought in. This time, spending topped revenue by about $5 billion, roughly half the prior shortfall.

The bill still shows up on the balance sheet. Debt, including finance leases, has climbed to nearly $39 billion from about $23 billion at the start of the year. Bond traders have noticed. The cost of insuring SpaceX's debt with credit default swaps hit a record this week, part of a broader AI credit scare that has hit names like CoreWeave ( CRWV ) even harder.

Musk isn't easing off. SpaceX ended the quarter with 1.7 gigawatts of computing capacity, and on the earnings call, he said he "would be surprised" if the company brought "less than 13 gigawatts of compute" online by the end of next year. That's more than seven times its current capacity, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.

He wants SpaceX running at a $100 billion annual revenue pace by year-end. It's at about $58 billion now, so December would have to look like a different company. Then again, so did this quarter.

articles.title: Meta and Google are about to have a consumer AI showdown
articles.summary: The companies poised for a heated confrontation over AI agents are also the two dominant digital advertising firms.
articles.body:
The race to put out a widely adopted and highly competent digital assistant is a fight to control the next popular tech platform . It just so happens that the companies poised for a heated confrontation over AI agents are also the two dominant digital advertising firms.

Meta ( META ), which reports quarterly results Tuesday, and Google ( GOOG ) are headed for an AI showdown.

Last month Meta's Muse burst onto the scene , delivering the first popular AI agent for normies, and just cracked a download milestone . Muse's early success, in both downloads and praise, previewed a world where more people rely on their digital helpers to get work done and manage their daily routines.

But even as billions of people are plugged into Meta's social networks — Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp — users don't depend on Meta in the same way they do Google and Apple ( AAPL ).

More cautious tech users might wait for the first wave of early adopters to find the bugs and iron out the kinks. The trust that goes with safeguarding emails, calendars, and wallets hasn't historically been Meta's purview. Better to hold out for whatever consumer-focused agent the iPhone maker or the Gmail company has in store.

First-mover status has won Meta public goodwill and an upward jolt in its stock price. Still, that hasn't made the threat from its advertising rival any less potent.

Several analysts have said that Google's future agent offering is a key risk facing Meta. Being first is often good enough in the tech world. But what comes second can be better — or more trusted. And in the uncharted territory of new AI services, early, tech-oriented users are likely to be different from the masses of people who enter the market later on.

"Google remains well positioned to lead in the AI era supported by proprietary models, custom silicon & broad product distribution," wrote Bank of America analysts led by Justin Post in a note earlier this week. He added that a competitive agent and broader Gemini 4 launch could be catalysts for the search giant.

Another point of tension between Meta and Google is how their legacy businesses can help or hurt their AI ambitions.

Google and Meta are the top dogs in the digital advertising market. They account for more than half of global ad revenue. But one of the crucial ideas behind AI agents is moving away from a screen-phone-app interface. Mobile apps prospered because they allowed for an easier, more intuitive form of computing. AI agents, taken to the extreme, promise to do away with computing altogether, or at least in the way we are used to.

articles.title: Why would Musk merge SpaceX and Tesla?
articles.summary: Oct 21 (Reuters) - Elon Musk believes a merger between Tesla and SpaceX is a good idea, he said on Tuesday, publicly backing an idea that would create one of...
articles.body:
Oct 21 (Reuters) - Elon Musk believes a merger between Tesla and SpaceX is a good idea, he said on Tuesday, publicly backing an idea that would create one of the most valuable companies in the world, worth about $3.5 trillion.

While electric-vehicle maker Tesla and rocket company SpaceX ‌were once seen as largely separate businesses, the lines between them have blurred as Musk expands into artificial intelligence, robotics, advanced manufacturing, satellite communications, and ‌computing infrastructure, including data centers on Earth and potentially in orbit.

Here's what a potential merger could mean:

A merger would create a single company at the center of Musk's long-term vision: an ​integrated technology and manufacturing empire spanning AI , energy, robotics, communications, and transportation on Earth and beyond.

"I do think there's a lot of merit to combining the companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity, and there's a lot to be gained from cooperating on developing superintelligence software, chip design, the Terafab obviously, robotics, mass-to-orbit with the Starmind constellation (of orbital data centers), connectivity," Musk said on Tuesday.

Bringing the companies together could also simplify decision-making. Many of Musk's projects already cut across multiple companies, requiring approvals from separate boards and shareholders. ‌A combined company would give management more freedom to deploy ⁠capital, engineering talent and infrastructure where it sees the greatest opportunity.

Musk has long argued that he needs greater influence over Tesla to pursue its AI and robotics strategy. He owns nearly a fifth of Tesla and holds voting control at SpaceX. A merger could consolidate ⁠his influence.

Tesla shareholders would gain access to SpaceX's rapidly growing Starlink broadband operation, launch services business and future space ventures. SpaceX investors would gain ownership of Tesla's vehicle, energy storage, autonomous driving and robotics businesses.

A merged company could also become one of the world's most valuable corporations, with a market value of about $3.5 trillion, combining leadership positions in ​automobiles, ​robotics, satellite communications, launch services, energy storage and AI infrastructure.

Supporters would likely argue that the combined ​company could allocate capital more efficiently across businesses that are increasingly ‌interdependent.

Critics, however, argue that investors would be assuming exposure to a much broader range of technical, regulatory and execution risks, some of which have little connection to one another.

articles.title: Over half of coal plants face critically low fuel stocks as demand surges
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India’s coal-fired power plants are running low on fuel, with nearly half holding coal that can generate power for fewer than three days.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s coal-fired power plants are running low on fuel, with nearly half holding coal that can generate power for fewer than three days.The squeeze is getting tighter, with the number of plants reporting critically low stocks climbing to 96 out of 191 as of October 19, up from 60 in mid-September, according to data from the Central Electricity Authority.Overall, coal stocks at power stations have fallen by about 5% since the beginning of October, as per a Reuters report.The shortage comes even as the coal ministry said last week that it had increased supplies to power plants. Hotter-than-usual weather linked to El Niño has pushed up electricity demand, while weaker monsoon rains have reduced hydropower generation.With less electricity coming from hydropower and more demand to meet, coal-fired plants are under greater pressure to keep the power flowing.Power demand rises as hydropower output fallsDaily peak electricity demand this year has been 45 gigawatts (GW) to 50 GW higher than a year earlier. Weaker monsoon rains have reduced hydropower generation, forcing India to rely more on coal-fired plants to meet demand.In September, the gap between electricity demand and supply rose to 560 million kilowatt-hours (kWh), the highest since August 2023. This happened even as coal-fired plants increased their output to meet rising demand.Coal-fired power generation rose 13.3% in September from a year earlier, while hydropower generation fell 20%, CEA data showed.Nearly 55% of India's power generation now comes from non-fossil fuel sources. However, the country still depends on coal-fired plants during periods of high demand because it lacks enough batteries to store electricity generated from clean energy sources.Government puts coal import plan on holdIndia has put on hold a proposal to ask power plants to import coal to refill their stocks, Bloomberg reported on Monday, citing people familiar with the discussions.The government had considered asking plants to mix imported coal with domestic supplies to ease the shortage. However, high international prices and a weaker rupee have made imports more expensive, prompting the government to shelve the plan, the report said.Instead, policymakers have asked state-owned Coal India Ltd to increase production and the railways to ensure coal reaches power stations on time, according to Bloomberg.Benchmark thermal coal prices are at their highest level in three years. A weaker rupee has added to import costs, while higher oil prices have increased India's energy import bill.India has previously asked power plants to import coal when domestic supplies were not enough. This time, the government has chosen to focus on increasing local production and improving transportation rather than making imports compulsory.The move comes after an order directing more than 100 captive coal-fired power plants to operate at full capacity from October 1 until the end of the year to meet expected growth in electricity demand.Coal stocks at their lowest in nearly five yearsCoal stocks at Indian power plants have fallen to their lowest level in nearly five years as rising electricity demand and lower hydropower generation put pressure on domestic supplies.Below-normal monsoon rainfall has reduced hydropower output, while higher temperatures beyond the summer months have increased electricity use for cooling and irrigation. This has added to the demand for coal and reduced stocks at power plants.India's electricity shortage in September was the worst for that month in nearly a decade.However, the pace at which coal stocks are falling has slowed in October. Bloomberg's calculations based on power ministry data showed that domestic coal-fired power plants recorded an average daily drop of around 48,000 tonnes in their stocks during the first 17 days of October. This was about a fifth of the daily decline recorded in September.The government expects electricity demand to ease as temperatures fall, giving coal stocks a chance to recover. Average temperatures are forecast to drop slightly over the next two weeks but are expected to remain above the 30-year average, according to the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts.Coal ministry says supplies have improvedEarlier this month, the ministry said that daily coal supplies to the power sector had increased by around 36% from September levels. It also said the pace at which stocks were falling had slowed. The ministry clarified that a plant classified as having “critical stock” is being flagged as a warning and does not necessarily mean the plant is running out of coal or is about to shut down.Plants with low stocks are being closely monitored, and supplies are being redirected to help ensure uninterrupted electricity generation, the ministry said. CEA data showed that 87 of 190 coal-fired power plants had critically low stocks on October 8, compared with 50 in the first week of September. These plants held 20.6 million tonnes of coal, just 33% of the recommended stock of 61.2 million tonnes.Coal transportation by rail has also improved. The ministry said rail loading averaged more than 465 rakes a day in October, with the target of 470 rakes met on three consecutive days. Coal supplies by road and other modes had also increased. The ministry said that keeping coal transportation at 465-475 rakes a day should help stabilise stocks and rebuild supplies ahead of festive-season, winter and next summer's demand.You use AI every day. articles.title: SpaceX earnings left one big question unanswered
articles.summary: Investors are getting curious where fresh funding will come from for SpaceX.
articles.body:
The moment is now for Elon Musk to dial back founder mode at SpaceX ( SPCX ) and dial back up something else he is very good at: charming visionary founder who is asking for large sums of capital from people who want entry to the Muskverse.

Because judging by Musk's commentary on his late Tuesday earnings call, he will need a lot of fresh capital to deliver on aggressive growth timelines for Terrafab, Starlink broadband and rocket reusability. Perhaps way more than most investors think.

"The earnings call served to amplify the enormous calls on capital that loom over the next few years (particularly in the AI segment)," Moffettnathson analyst Julie Zhu said in a note. "SpaceX has moved at a frenetic pace over the last few months, closing the Cursor acquisition; announcing a new Starbase in Louisiana; winning yet another large IaaS contract; launching Starship flight 14; and purchasing Grain's 800 MHz spectrum. Each of these announcements portends an enormous amount of spending, both capex and opex, ahead.

Zhu calls out several specifics on the funding front:

"In the Space segment, Starship continues to require significant R&D. Starbase Louisiana has a reported price tag of $100B+. "

"Within the AI segment, the implied ramp in compute over the coming years will cost hundreds of billions of dollars. Management has also discussed building a foundry for gasturbine blades and vanes in Bastrop to help support power infrastructure. And that is just for training and inference that takes place on the ground; orbital compute at scale will require a separate envelope of expenditure."

"Further, we have yet to mention the R&D that is likely required to push Grok to the frontier."

"A terrestrial buildout for Starlink Mobile's D2D ambitions would require tens of billions, or more, for ground infrastructure and additional spectrum, and still more in start-up costs (think handset subsidies)."

SpaceX gave investors a taste of what could be to come on the debt funding front.

Execs guided to $35 billion to $40 billion in capex for the fourth quarter. This would be a meaningful step-up from $19.6 billion in the third quarter, $18.4 billion in the second quarter and $10.1 billion in the first quarter.

SpaceX ended the quarter with $36.1 billion in debt.

The company's veteran CFO Bret Johnson doesn't seem fazed by the tremors in the debt markets of late on concerns over the financial health of neoclouds such as CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Nebius ( NBIS ).

All systems go on the pursuit of capital, or so it appears.

articles.title: Explained: How capital gains tax works on stocks, mutual funds, property and gold
articles.summary: By Archit Gupta Most investors spend weeks deciding what to buy. Very few spend even an hour planning how they will sell.
articles.body: By Archit GuptaMost investors spend weeks deciding what to buy. Very few spend even an hour planning how they will sell. Yet the tax on an investment is charged when you realize your gains, not when you deploy your capital.This gap matters today more than ever. India now accounts for over 23 crore demat accounts, and millions of middle-class families hold gold or property that they will eventually monetize. Capital gains tax is no longer an exclusive concern for high-net-worth individuals.A few years ago, capital gains appeared mostly in the tax returns of seasoned traders and business owners. Today, salaried professionals with a basic SIP, a small equity portfolio, or an inherited apartment routinely encounter these provisions. Unfortunately, many learn the operational rules only after executing a sale.My view on this is simple. The best time to plan for capital gains tax is before you place a sell order, and ideally when you make the initial investment. The foundational rules are clear, and a small amount of advance planning can reduce your tax outflow significantly.This year is a good time to revisit the rules. From April 1, 2026, the Income-tax Act, 2025 has replaced the 1961 law. Section numbers have changed and the law now uses the term tax year, but capital gains are taxed largely as before.Short-Term versus Long-Term ClassificationEvery capital gains calculation begins with a single variable: holding duration.Listed shares, equity mutual funds, and listed securities such as gold ETFs transition into long-term assets after 12 months. Immovable property, physical gold, unlisted shares, and non-equity mutual funds require a holding duration of 24 months to qualify as long-term assets.Two critical nuances are often overlooked during portfolio reviews:Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs): Each monthly instalment carries its own distinct acquisition date. The law applies First-In, First-Out (FIFO) accounting, treating the earliest acquired units as the first sold.Inherited or Gifted Assets: When you inherit property or receive an asset from a relative, both the holding period and the original cost of acquisition transfer to you from the previous owner.Equities and Mutual Funds: Timing Your ExitsIn equity markets, holding duration dictates net returns. Selling a profitable equity mutual fund one week before it completes 12 months triggers a Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) tax rate of 20%. Holding that same fund for one additional week subjects the gain to the Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) rate of 12.5%, while unlocking an annual tax-free threshold.The Rs 1.25 lakh annual LTCG exemption under Section 112A remains one of the most effective tax-planning tools available to retail investors. It applies cumulatively across listed shares and equity mutual funds. Unused portions of this limit lapse at the end of each financial year.Harvesting gains systematically by selling sufficient units each year to utilize the Rs 1.25 lakh threshold, then reinvesting the proceeds, resets your cost basis higher and lowers future taxable gains. Investors should account for exit loads and transaction charges before executing this maneuver.Gold, Real Estate, and Fixed Income AssetsHolding period classifications govern taxation across non-equity assets:General Rule: Long-term gains on real estate, physical gold, and unlisted securities incur a flat tax rate of 12.5%. Short-term gains are added directly to your taxable income and taxed at your applicable personal slab rate.Debt Mutual Funds: Units in debt schemes investing over 65% in debt instruments acquired on or after April 1, 2023, do not qualify for long-term tax rates. All realized gains are treated as short-term income and taxed at your income tax slab rate, regardless of holding duration.Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs): While fresh tranches ceased issuing in early 2024, secondary market and historical holdings remain active. Gains realized upon maturity are tax-exempt solely for original subscribers who hold the bonds through redemptions with the Reserve Bank of India. Bonds purchased on stock exchanges or transferred prior to maturity remain taxable.The Rs 12 Lakh Tax Rebate MisconceptionA widespread belief among salaried taxpayers is that total income up to Rs 12 lakh is completely tax-free under the current tax regime. This assumption breaks down when capital gains are subject to special tax rates.Consider a professional earning a taxable salary of Rs 12 lakh who realizes a Rs 1 lakh short-term gain on equity shares. While the salary component receives rebate benefits, the Rs 1 lakh short-term gain is taxed independently at 20% plus applicable cess. Special capital gains tax rates operate uniformly across both old and new tax regimes.Conversely, resident individuals with limited primary income can offset unutilized portions of their basic exemption limit against capital gains. A retired parent with zero taxable income can realize up to Rs 4 lakh in long-term equity gains under the new regime without triggering net tax liability.Property Transactions and Indexation OptionsReal estate transactions require careful planning due to the scale of capital involved. Under current regulations, resident individuals and Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs) selling residential properties acquired before July 23, 2024, can choose between two tax computation methods. They are permitted to pay the lower of 12.5% without indexation or 20% with indexation.Indexation does not automatically guarantee a lower tax burden. Selecting the optimal method depends on how your property's appreciation compares to official inflation metrics:When Indexation Helps (20% Rate): When the holding period is very long, since the property acquisition date is early. In these cases, the benefit of indexation beats the benefit of the reduced tax rate at 12.5%When Unindexed Flat Rate Helps (12.5% Rate): When the holding period is relatively shorter, where the reduced tax rate is more beneficial, as compared to applying indexation with 20% tax rateReinvesting to save taxTaxpayers can neutralize long-term capital gains tax by reinvesting their gains:Section 54 (Residential Real Estate): Capital gains from selling a residential property are exempt if reinvested into another residential house in India. The replacement property must be acquired within 1 year before or 2 years after the sale, or constructed within 3 years. The exemption is capped at Rs 10 crore. Taxpayers realizing gains up to Rs 2 crore can exercise a one-time lifetime option to invest in two residential properties.Section 54F (Non-Residential Assets): Selling non-residential assets (such as equity shares, gold, or commercial plots) and reinvesting into a residential house qualifies for tax relief. To secure a 100% exemption, the entire net sale consideration must be reinvested. Investing a portion yields a proportional exemption. Claimants must not own more than one residential house on the transaction date.Section 54EC (Capital Gains Bonds): Real estate investors can deploy up to Rs 50 lakh of long-term gains into designated infrastructure bonds (issued by REC, PFC, or IRFC) within 6 months of sale. These bonds offer a 5.25% annual return, carry a 5-year lock-in period, and generate taxable interest income.For Sections 54 and 54F, disposing of the new residential property within 3 years revokes the exemption. If suitable property acquisitions cannot be finalized before the tax return filing deadline, funds must be deposited into the Capital Gains Account Scheme (CGAS) with a scheduled bank to retain tax relief.Real estate involves long-term operational commitments. Acquiring real estate solely to save tax is rarely optimal. If homeownership does not fit your operational goals, infrastructure bonds provide a cleaner capital preservation vehicle despite the Rs 50 lakh limit.Loss Set-Off and Carry-Forward ExecutionManaging capital losses effectively preserves portfolio yield. A Short-Term Capital Loss (STCL) can offset both short-term and long-term capital gains across any asset class. A Long-Term Capital Loss (LTCL) can only offset long-term capital gains.Capital losses cannot reduce salary or business income. Unabsorbed losses can be carried forward for up to 8 consecutive tax years, provided the original income tax return is filed on or before the statutory due date. Missing the filing deadline forfeits loss carry-forward privileges permanently.Pre-Exit Planning ChecklistNet returns are governed by post-tax capital retention. Two investors can acquire the same asset on the same date and realize identical gross profits, yet experience significantly different net outcomes based on exit execution.Before executing a sale across any asset class, evaluate purchase timestamps, compute alternative tax scenarios, and establish target reinvestment channels. Strategic exit planning remains a high-return exercise in personal finance.Making Exit Planning Your AdvantageFor too long, investors have treated capital gains tax as an unexpected bill after selling. In reality, what you keep after tax is the true measure of your investment success.As Indian families build wealth across shares, property, and gold under the Income-tax Act, 2025, exit planning is no longer optional. It is a necessary financial habit.By tracking your purchase dates, using annual tax-free limits, and checking reinvestment options before you sell, you can save a significant amount of tax. Before you place your next sell order, take a few minutes to calculate your post-tax return. Those few minutes will pay off better than almost any other financial decision you make.The author is Founder and CEO, ClearTaxYou use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Nvidia reveals plans for 'an AI factory in a shipping container' to build data centers in weeks, not months
articles.summary: Nvidia debuted its DSX POD at GTC Berlin on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Nvidia ( NVDA ) wants to reduce the time it takes for its customers to start generating revenue from its AI systems.

At its GTC event in Berlin on Wednesday, the company unveiled its DSX POD, a reference design for an AI data center packed into a box about the size of a standard shipping container.

Data center construction can take months, if not years, to get up and running. And because they don't start generating revenue until they begin processing AI tokens, the longer a data center takes to come online, the more expenses pile up.

The DSX POD is meant to serve as a faster, modular solution for companies that need access to data center capabilities sooner rather than later.

"The moment then you have to install these AI factories, and they're gigantic. And putting these AI factories into service takes months. If we could reduce that months, you know, from the moment that the systems are shipped to the moment that it's deployed and being operational, if we could reduce it from months to weeks or even a month, that will be completely game-changing for all of these AI factories," CEO Jensen Huang told Deirdre Bosa.

According to Nvidia, the Vera Rubin-powered DSX PODs will arrive on site, ready to be plugged into the power, cooling, and networking infrastructure, reducing deployment time from six months to 14 days.

The company said DSX PODs won't replace traditional data centers, but will serve as a means to start running AI applications before brick-and-mortar facilities are ready.

"With Nvidia DSX POD, we're bringing factory-built precision and speed to AI infrastructure construction — reducing deployment time from months to weeks so customers can scale capacity and bring revenue-generating production online faster," Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said in a statement.

According to the company, the DSX POD supports liquid cooling, but because it uses dry-cooler designs, it can save up to 54 million liters of water per day versus a standard data center.

Standing up data centers more quickly doesn't just help Nvidia's customers, though. Faster data center deployment should ease at least one of the chokepoints in the AI build-out, which means faster chip sales for Nvidia.

Semiconductors aren't the only bottleneck for data center builders. Getting the electricity necessary to power those processors is also a concern. And power plants take far longer to construct than data centers.

articles.title: How tokenised equities are reshaping global investment  access for market participants
articles.summary: The global financial system is undergoing a fundamental transformation driven by the integration of digital infrastructure with traditional asset classes.
articles.body: The global financial system is undergoing a fundamental transformation driven by the integration of digital infrastructure with traditional asset classes. At the forefront of this evolution is the rapid expansion of real-world assets (RWA)-traditional financial instruments that have been digitized for blockchain-based trading. This sector has seen explosive growth, with tokenised equities leading the thirty-day inflows across the broader digital asset ecosystem. The active market for these digitised assets has recently surpassed the $30 billion mark, representing an increase of roughly six times its 2024 level, according to industry reporting by CoinDesk. This massive capital influx signals a structural shift in how global investors prefer to access and utilise established financial instruments.The limitations of traditional equity marketsFor decades, traditional equity markets have operated under a rigid set of constraints that limit global participation. Investors are bound by regional exchange hours, meaning that market-moving news often occurs when venues are closed. Furthermore, the operational friction of moving capital across borders and dealing with delayed settlement times has created artificial barriers to entry.In conventional markets, holding a stock is generally a passive endeavour. Using stock portfolios as direct collateral for other trading activities is a privilege typically reserved for massive institutional players, leaving retail participants with highly inefficient capital structures.How tokenisation solves structural inefficienciesThe tokenisation of equities solves these structural inefficiencies by moving traditional shares onto blockchain networks. By creating a digital representation of a real-world asset, tokenisation allows for continuous, round-the-clock trading that is not dependent on traditional market hours or geographies. These digitised shares can be moved instantly, stored in l wallets, and integrated into decentralised finance applications. More importantly, they transform passive holdings into active financial tools, allowing investors to maintain exposure to premium assets while simultaneously using those assets as collateral within broader digital ecosystems.The accelerated adoption of Binance bStocksRecognising the overwhelming demand for continuous market access, Binance entered the tokenised equity space and immediately set new industry benchmarks. The company launched bStocks, its tokenised equities stocks and exchange-traded funds, on June 11 (available only for select jurisdictions), and the product has seen extraordinary adoption¹. The platform's offering grew significantly faster in its first month than competing products like xStocks did in the same window, with Binance passing the month-five total of xStocks inside its first two months¹. This trajectory propelled bStocks to become the fastest tokenised equity product in history to surpass $1 billion in assets under management, reaching this milestone roughly four months after its initial launch¹.The underlying volume and user metrics paint a clear picture of how rapidly participants are embracing this new market structure. Within just 24 days of launching, the product generated an impressive $1.8 billion in trading volume¹. This activity rose sharply throughout the summer, hitting $14.7 billion in July across the Binance spot market and the BNB Chain¹. According to research from Delphi Digital, nearly 300,000 individual people had traded these digitised equities by the end of that month³.Bridging traditional and digital ecosystemsThe true measure of success for any financial product is its sustained usage. Behind the headline assets under management figure sits more than $40 billion in cumulative trading volume across nearly 100 listed tokens¹. Furthermore, the system has successfully processed $6 billion in conversions at a strict 1:1 ratio with direct stock holdings¹. Each digitised share on the platform is fully backed by the underlying security and redeems directly into the actual stock itself, rather than settling merely for its cash equivalent¹.This precise structural design ensures deep, continuous liquidity and fosters immense trust. "bStocks is showing how tokenized equities can open a more connected and accessible path to global markets," stated Shunyet Jan, Head of Exchange and Trading at Binance. "Users want to access traditional assets alongside the digital assets they already hold, trade beyond conventional market hours and move between products with less operational friction. By the end of July, there were more than 400,000 on-chain bStocks trader, excluding off-chain centralized exchange trading, showing how quickly interest developed in the first weeks following launch. These are early signals, but they show how existing market infrastructure and a global user base can help tokenised equities develop deeper participation and more continuous liquidity¹."Redefining utility and collateral efficiencyPerhaps the most significant innovation introduced by this product line is how it reimagines the utility of equity holdings. In traditional finance, brokerages typically only accept cash or highly liquid cash equivalents as collateral for retail margin borrowing. Conversely, these tokenised equities operate around the clock and actively function as collateral for retail users, marking a massive point of differentiation from conventional market structures¹.This functional utility proves that digitised shares are becoming an enduring, foundational layer of the modern economy. "The test of a tokenized stock isn't the launch-day chart; it's whether it still behaves like a market after the launch," noted Shunyet Jan. "bStocks trade around the clock, get used as collateral, move between wallets, and convert 1:1 into direct stock holdings. Today, more than a billion dollars of that is held on Binance, and it's being used, not just held¹."The future of borderless, 24/7 equity marketsAs global investors increasingly demand flexibility, transparency, and capital efficiency, tokenised equities are emerging as a critical bridge between traditional finance and the digital asset ecosystem. For the tech-forward investor community, products like bStocks represent the natural evolution of how financial markets should operate in a connected, digital-first world.References:Binance Blog. articles.title: Playing doubles with AI: How human judgement becomes the winning partner
articles.summary: LONDON: As businesses accelerate the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), industry leaders have stressed the importance of human judgement, trusted
articles.body: LONDON: As businesses accelerate the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), industry leaders have stressed the importance of human judgement, trusted data and strong governance in turning technological capabilities into meaningful business outcomes.The issue was central to Elevate Connect London 2026, the flagship event organised by Mumbai-based IT multinational ADROSONIC for senior leaders in the UK insurance market. Held at the Four Seasons Hotel London at Tower Bridge, the invitation-only gathering focused on the theme “AI Predicts. Humans Decide.”Discussions covered AI adoption, data quality, business transformation and leadership, with speakers emphasising that technology alone cannot deliver value without human expertise and organisational readiness.‘AI should complement human capabilities’One of the key sessions was a fireside conversation titled “Playing Doubles with AI”, featuring Mayank, founder and CEO of ADROSONIC, and Hasani Jess, group CTO of Aventum Group.Drawing on the example of tennis legend Leander Paes, Mayank compared effective human-AI collaboration to a doubles partnership, where complementary strengths matter more than identical capabilities.“Great doubles partnerships are not built by finding someone identical to you,” Mayank said. “They are built by combining complementary strengths and compensating for one another’s weaknesses.”He cited Paes’s career to illustrate how ambition, context and human judgement can defy expectations based solely on data. While AI can process information, conduct research and improve efficiency, people must interpret that information and decide how to act on it.Jess said effective AI use requires practice and expertise, despite the technology’s apparent accessibility.“AI is intoxicatingly familiar,” he said. “It looks easy because we can all interact with it. But just as watching a professional athlete is very different from performing at that level, working effectively with AI requires discipline, learning and experience.”The speakers also discussed the importance of trust, noting that confidence in AI systems must develop through repeated use and demonstrated reliability. With models evolving rapidly, organisations must continually reassess how best to combine human and machine capabilities.For Mayank, the real opportunity lies in using AI to achieve outcomes that would otherwise be beyond an organisation’s reach.“If AI is only helping us do the same things faster, that is one plus one equals two,” he said. “The real opportunity comes when AI enables us to do things we could not do before. That is when one plus one becomes eleven.”Business context and governance key to scaling AIAnother panel examined how businesses can expand AI adoption while protecting human expertise, governance and client trust.James Welch, head of delivery at Miller, said AI deployment must reflect the risks associated with individual business functions.While high-risk areas such as claims and payments require strong human oversight, tasks such as generating renewal packs could benefit significantly from automation. He added that protecting the company’s brand, expertise and client relationships remained a priority.Nitin Agrawal, lead business architect at ADROSONIC, said adoption, rather than technology, was often the biggest challenge.He stressed the need to redesign operating models, upskill employees and involve business users in developing AI initiatives.Daniel Del Moro, director of AI and automation innovation at UiPath, highlighted the importance of reliable data and well-defined processes.He cautioned against treating AI as a cure-all, arguing that businesses must first address process inefficiencies and data-quality problems. Combining established technologies such as robotic process automation (RPA) with newer AI tools could help unlock greater value, he said.The panel’s broader message was that AI adoption should be treated as a business transformation programme, supported by leadership, change management, clear accountability and end-to-end objectives, rather than as an isolated technology project.How much Data Quality is enough for AI?Data readiness was another focus, with leaders from AUB Group, Hampden Risk Partners, Oneglobal Broking and ADROSONIC discussing how businesses can establish reliable data foundations without delaying AI projects in pursuit of perfect information.The panel agreed that data should be trustworthy, understood and fit for the decision it is intended to support.Raj Rai said competitive advantage would depend not merely on adopting AI, but on understanding data quality, lineage, governance and how the technology is applied within an organisation.Ben Ormerod noted that the level of data quality required depends on the decision being made. Although AI can accelerate business outcomes, poor-quality inputs can also speed up poor decisions. He also highlighted AI’s potential to identify data-quality issues and trace data lineage.Marc Steel said AI should support rather than replace human expertise, particularly in relationship-driven sectors such as specialty insurance, where client relationships and market context remain important.Kamlesh Yadav cautioned that confidence expressed by AI systems should not be mistaken for accuracy. He emphasised the need for trusted information, clear ownership, human oversight and measurable business outcomes.The discussion highlighted the need to balance experimentation with safeguards, ensuring that innovation does not come at the expense of security, accountability or sound decision-making.Polar explorer draws parallels with business leadershipThe event also featured a keynote by polar explorer Ann Daniels, who drew on her expeditions across the Arctic and Antarctica to discuss leadership, resilience and decision-making under uncertainty.Daniels described operating in environments where conditions can change without warning, resources are limited and decisions can have serious consequences. In such situations, success depends on preparation, teamwork and the ability to adapt when plans no longer work.Her experiences offered parallels with the challenges facing businesses as AI capabilities, market expectations and competitive pressures evolve. Just as polar explorers must reassess conditions and adjust their routes, business leaders must make decisions without always having complete information.Daniels emphasised that technology and data can support decisions, but leaders still need to judge when and how to act on the information available. Her keynote reinforced the event’s broader focus on adaptability, collaboration and human judgement during periods of change.A Boardroom Live session also examined a proposal to expand ADROSONIC’s Digital Innovation Lab at BIT Mesra.Across the sessions, speakers returned to a common theme: AI’s value depends not only on what the technology can do, but also on the quality of the data, processes and decisions surrounding it.As organisations move beyond experimentation, effective adoption will require combining technological capability with human expertise, clear governance and trust.You use AI every day.
