articles.title: The iPhone Duo is Apple’s coolest phone in years. There’s just one problem
articles.summary: There were many times I didn’t want to put the iPhone Duo down. Once you get used to reading, watching TV and scrolling through Instagram on a giant screen, it’s hard to go back to a tiny glowing rectangle.
articles.body: There were many times I didn’t want to put the iPhone Duo down. Once you get used to reading, watching TV and scrolling through Instagram on a giant screen, it’s hard to go back to a tiny glowing rectangle. There’s just one issue: Many apps are still made for that little rectangle. This is what it’s been like to use the iPhone Duo, Apple’s first foldable iPhone, which launches on October 23. It starts at $2,000, making it as expensive as Apple’s latest 14-inch MacBook Pro. It’s a big move for Apple, which rarely messes with the winning formula that’s turned the iPhone into a business that raked in more than $200 billion in revenue last year. But after years of incremental iPhone updates, Apple faced pressure to prove it could still captivate consumers. I got a taste of that future after spending about a week with the new foldable phone that Apple provided CNN for testing purposes. The iPhone Duo became my tablet for watching Netflix, a bedside alarm clock at night, an extra screen for watching football on Sunday, a miniature monitor when connected to my Bluetooth keyboard and a camera with a built-in tripod. But there were equally as many times – if not more – when I grew frustrated because apps didn’t work the way they should, since developers haven’t updated them yet. And despite Apple’s “it just works” approach, the iPhone Duo takes some getting used to. While the iPhone Duo’s software certainly felt much smoother and more fluid than Android alternatives, many of its core features have been available on Samsung or Google phones for years. What can iPhone Duo do that a regular phone can’t? The iPhone Duo is the biggest change Apple has made to the iPhone in its nearly 20-year history. There’s a 5.4-inch screen on the outside, which unfolds to reveal a 7.6-inch display on the inside. When closed, the iPhone Duo feels like a passport, but obviously thicker and heavier. When opened, it’s like a thinner and smaller iPad Mini. One of the most popular questions I get about the iPhone Duo is whether you see the crease. The answer, believe it or not, is no. The crease is barely visible when using apps or scrolling around the home screen, and I can hardly feel it when swiping across the display. The iPhone Duo’s unconventional shape means it can do things you wouldn’t be able to do as easily with a regular phone. Prop it open like a tent or stand it up like a book while the screen is locked, and the display will turn into a bedside clock, digital photo frame or calendar. Certain apps like the camera and Apple Fitness Plus will shift to the top portion of the screen when folded halfway like a laptop – but that depends on whether developers program their apps to do it. When the phone is open, you can take selfies with the phone’s rear cameras while viewing a preview on the cover screen, which came in handy when I was shooting the video for this review. The iPhone Duo can run two apps on screen at the same time, which was useful for situations that involved looking up information or viewing content in multiple apps. You can, for example, drag and drop an image straight from the Photos app into a text message when both apps are on screen. I also used split screen mode to show a friend my Halloween costume and the movie character it’s based on at the same time. While this is convenient, it’s probably not the reason you’re going to buy an iPhone Duo. The Duo’s inner screen is best used when dedicating the whole thing to a single app like Netflix. And the display has a matte finish, which reduces glare and doesn’t smudge easily. But many apps, including popular ones like Google Maps, Gmail, Call of Duty Mobile, and Uber weren’t updated to take full advantage of this big screen when I tested the Duo before launch. Some apps looked like floating windows in the middle of the tablet-sized screen. These apps can expand to occupy more of the display, but they still don’t fill the whole space. Other apps were updated to occupy most of the display but still had a black bar along the side. That’s what you see when developers haven’t updated their apps using Apple’s latest software development tools, as the company lays out on its website. The good news is that more apps have been updated even during the few days I’ve had the phone, including Google, TikTok, Instagram and Threads. But the uncertainty of not knowing how an app is going to look feels inconsistent and can be jarring – which is an area where Android has had a head start. The apps that are optimized for the Duo provide a glimpse of what’s possible. My favorite app so far is the puzzle platform game Planet of Lana, which looks gorgeous and colorful on the Duo’s larger screen. I also really liked using Apple Books, which lets you view pages on either side of the screen when the display is slightly folded like a real book. (Amazon’s Kindle app is one of the many apps that hasn’t been updated yet). Apple’s Messages and Mail apps also show your inbox on the left and messages on the right so that you can see everything at once. But how is it as a regular phone? For its price, the iPhone Duo should be able to do everything a regular phone can do and more. My biggest concern was that the design would make it feel awkward to use when closed, but typing and swiping on the cover screen feels surprisingly natural and comfortable. I’ve even come to prefer the Duo’s wider keyboard over the one on my iPhone 18 Pro. Still, there was a learning curve at first. I kept accidentally hitting the Siri button, which is located on the Duo’s side, when I meant to press the volume keys on the top of the phone. I also didn’t realize that you must have an app open before you can use split screen mode, rather than just opening a new app and dragging it to one side of the display from the home screen. Battery life is reasonable and in line with what you’d expect from a new phone. My battery was usually down to 35% or 46% by the time I went to bed, although that will always vary depending on which apps you’re using and how often you’re using the tablet screen compared to the cover display. The iPhone Duo has cameras that are similar to the iPhone 18 Pro’s but with one key difference: there’s no telephoto camera. That means zoomed-in photos won’t look as crisp or clear compared to ones taken on the iPhone 18 Pro, although shots captured on both phones looked similar otherwise. The biggest question I get about the iPhone Duo is whether it’s worth the $2,000. That’s tough to answer considering it costs more than a month’s rent for most Americans . The only reason you should even consider it is if you really want a screen that’s bigger than you’d find on any other phone but still fits in your pocket. My advice? Wait until developers have had more time to optimize their apps before you decide. While the Duo is compelling, apps still have catching up to do.

articles.title: Civil servant admits he 'made mistakes' juggling five government jobs
articles.summary: Kashim Chowdhury was contracted for 183 hours a week, more than the number of hours in seven days.
articles.body:
The civil servant accused of fraudulently earning more than £284,000 by juggling multiple public-sector jobs admitted making mistakes but said ''I do not believe there was criminal intent".

Giving evidence at Southwark Crown Court, Kashim Chowdhury told the jury he had made mistakes because he was ''overwhelmed and stressed'' and had felt ''terror and panic'' at the thought of losing his livelihood.

He told the jury he had been diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder in 2015 and that it had been triggered in 2021.

The 55-year-old, who is from east London, is on trial accused of nine counts of fraud. He denies acting dishonestly or intending to make a dishonest gain.

The prosecution alleges Chowdhury failed to reveal to his employers that he had other full-time employment. But Chowdhury told the jury some of his managers knew he had other jobs.

His managers at Department for Environment and Rural Affairs (Defra), the London Borough of Tower Hamlets, East London NHS Trust and the Department for Health and Social Care (DHSC) all knew he had other jobs.

The prosecution alleges that at the height of the deceit, Chowdhury held five full-time jobs on full-time salaries within the public sector.

In the spring of 2023, he was employed by Defra, the UK Health Security Agency, the Food Standards Agency, the Department for Business and Trade and the Home Office. The jury was told that throughout this period he was contracted to work 183 hours a week - more than the number of hours that exist in seven days.

Each job paid a full-time wage, with Chowdhury paid £11,000 for a single month's work in 2023.

The prosecution alleges Chowdhury managed to keep his overlapping jobs secret because he worked entirely remotely. He told his employers he was the sole carer for his elderly mother and the prosecution alleges he "exploited this opportunity".

A succession of Chowdhury's line managers have told the jury that he performed poorly in his roles.

Abigail Mounde, who was Chowdhury's line manager at the Department for Business and Trade told the court: ''Any basic tasks I asked him to do he either did late or not to the standard I would have expected."

The prosecution also alleges Chowdhury used sick notes from his doctor as part of the cover-up.

But the court was told that while he was telling some employers he was sick and unfit to work because of "mixed anxiety and depressive disorder" he was not giving sick notes to other employers. The prosecution said this ''underlines the dishonesty involved in the whole affair".

His line manager at the Health Security Agency, Aleesha Adams, arranged a video call in May 2023, to support him returning to work after a period of absence.

She said she was surprised when he logged on wearing white make-up because his name led her to expect to see an Asian man with darker skin.

She told the court that as the call went on the make-up started coming off his forehead. ''He was sweating, it was like rubbing off so it was darker underneath and darker on the neck."

Prosecuting barrister Lucy Organ told the court: ''This almost laughable incident demonstrates quite how far the defendant was willing to go in his deceit.''

articles.title: Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat sleeper train may launch on November 1; journey time may fall from 24 hours to 16 and fares for 1,118 km trip could range from Rs 2,600 to Rs 4,250
articles.summary: Indian Railways’ second Vande Bharat sleeper train service is all set to start in the coming days.
articles.body: Indian Railways’ second Vande Bharat sleeper train service is all set to start in the coming days. South Western Railway (SWR) has proposed November 1, the occasion of Karnataka Rajyotsava, for the inaugural special run of the new Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper Express.The date on which the train will begin regular commercial operations, however, has not yet been announced. According to SWR sources, Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw is likely to flag off the service. It will be the first Vande Bharat sleeper train to operate in southern India.Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat sleeper train: Likely Timings and FareThe train, likely to be numbered 27651/27652, will have 16 coaches, including 11 AC three-tier coaches, four AC two-tier coaches and one AC first-class coach. Together, they will provide a total of 823 berths.Tickets for the 1,118-km journey could cost between Rs 2,600 and Rs 4,250, with the fare varying according to the class selected. The railway authorities have yet to release the final fare details.It was earlier reported that the Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat sleeper is likely to leave KSR Bengaluru at 10 PM and arrive at Mumbai's CSMT at 1:50 PM the following day. On the return journey, it could depart CSMT at 10:30 PM and reach Bengaluru at 2:50 PM. However, the timings have not been finalised yet.The new train is expected to cut travel time considerably between Bengaluru and Mumbai, a route that has long been without a quicker overnight rail option. The Udyan Express, the main daily direct service connecting the two cities, currently takes approximately 24 hours to complete the journey. The proposed Vande Bharat Sleeper Express is expected to bring the travel time down to around 16 hours.The planned route will cover Anantapur, Guntakal, Raichur, Kalaburagi, Solapur and Kalyan before arriving in Mumbai.An official said the service could not be introduced in October because the model code of conduct was in force for the Karnataka legislative council elections.What sets the Vande Bharat sleeper apart?The Vande Bharat sleeper train has a 16-coach configuration, comprising 11 AC three-tier coaches, four AC two-tier coaches and one AC First Class coach.Designed for operations at speeds of up to 160 kmph, the train has a maximum testing speed of 180 kmph, placing it in the semi-high-speed category. However, much of the Indian Railways network currently lacks the infrastructure needed to support train operations at these speeds.The new train is a much superior travel experience compared to Rajdhani Express trains. The coaches incorporate design features inspired by European trains, including cushioned berths intended to make overnight journeys more comfortable. The upper berths have also been redesigned to make access easier for passengers.Several facilities have been incorporated to improve the onboard experience. These include dedicated night lights, a public announcement system integrated with visual displays, CCTV surveillance and modular pantry units.The train features modern bio-vacuum toilets of the kind used in aircraft. It also has a separate toilet for passengers with disabilities, equipped with a baby care station. Those travelling in AC First Class will have access to showers with hot water.On the safety front, the sleeper variant is equipped with the indigenous KAVACH anti-collision system. It will also feature regenerative braking, a technology used in Vande Bharat chair car trains to improve energy efficiency.Automatic doors connect the coaches, while fully sealed gangways help keep the interiors clean and maintain temperature control throughout the train.Each coach is fitted with individual reading lights, charging points and refreshment tables. GFRP panels have been used for the interiors, and the train's doors are designed to open automatically at designated stations.Other features include a Centralised Coach Monitoring System and an emergency communication facility through which passengers can contact the driver directly when necessary.Separately, the Integral Coach Factory (ICF) is developing its own version of the Vande Bharat sleeper train.You use AI every day. articles.title: Supermicro stock jumps as server maker lifts revenue forecast
articles.summary: Supermicro stock jumped in early trading as the company upped its gross margin guidance amid a record backlog of orders.
articles.body:
What happened: Supermicro ( SMCI ) stock jumped 12% in early trading on Wednesday, while peers Dell Technologies ( DELL ) and Hewlett Packard Enterprise ( HPE ) gained 5% and 4%, respectively.

What's behind the move: The AI server maker raised its fiscal first quarter revenue forecast by $4 billion, signaling stronger-than-expected demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Supermicro now expects revenue of $18.5 billion to $19.5 billion for the quarter ended Sept. 30, up from its previous forecast of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion.

The company also raised its gross margin forecast to 12% to 12.5%, compared with its previous outlook of 10.4% to 10.8%, citing a more favorable customer and product mix.

Supermicro will present its complete Q1 fiscal year 2027 financial results on Nov. 3.

What else you need to know: Supermicro designs and builds servers and data center systems that incorporate semiconductors from chipmakers like Nvidia ( NVDA ), Intel ( INTC ), and AMD ( AMD ).

Supermicro's update comes as investors weigh the AI trade, signaling that demand for hardware remains robust, even as questions persist about the returns on massive data-center investments.

The rally also puts AI-related stocks back in focus following SpaceX's ( SPCX ) AI-driven results.

Year to date, Supermicro stock is up roughly 10%.

articles.title: How continuing to work will impact your Social Security check next year
articles.summary: Last week, the SSA announced that the 2027 annual earnings ceiling for those under full retirement age who are receiving Social Security benefits will increa...
articles.body:
Claiming Social Security while still on the job is increasingly common, but there are rules to be aware of to avoid a surprise when your monthly check arrives.

"Most retirees need to supplement their Social Security because the benefits aren't large enough to cover typical living expenses," Richard Johnson, AARP's vice president of financial security, told Yahoo Finance.

You can take Social Security as early as age 62, but your benefit can be reduced by as much as 30% compared to what it would be at your full retirement age (FRA). For anyone born in 1960 or later, your FRA is 67.

If you delay benefits from your FRA until age 70, you earn delayed retirement credits. Those come to roughly an 8% increase in your benefit for each year until you hit 70, when the credits stop accruing.

Here's the catch: If you continue to earn income after claiming Social Security benefits after age 62 and before your FRA, the Social Security Administration (SSA) will temporarily withhold a portion of your benefits for earnings over a certain threshold.

It's not as simple as you might think it should be. In general, $1 is withheld for every $2 earned above the limit until the year you hit your full retirement age.

Last week, the SSA announced that the 2027 annual earnings ceiling for those under full retirement age will increase to $25,560 from $24,480 this year.

In the year you hit full retirement age, that limit increases in 2027 to $67,920 for earnings made in months prior to the month you hit your full retirement age. In the month you hit full retirement age, the annual earnings test ends.

From then on, you can earn without restriction, and while you don't get the amount you forfeited previously in a lump sum, your monthly benefit is adjusted upward, so you recoup all the benefits that were withheld.

The earnings calculation does not count income from pensions, annuities, investment income such as interest, dividends, capital gains, and IRA or retirement account withdrawals.

You can use the SSA's calculator to walk through your scenario.

"We've built a system that practically guarantees that people will have to keep working after they claim," said Bradley Schurman, demographic strategist and author of "The Super Age." "A 3.6% COLA helps, but it trails prices for a lot of retirees."

Inflation is running hotter than it has in a few years, and it's hitting the things older households can't cut back on: housing, food, insurance, and healthcare, he added.

articles.title: EBay to Cut 9% of Staff to Streamline Operations, Reuters Says
articles.summary: EBay Inc. will eliminate 9% of its workforce in an effort to streamline operations and prioritize its best-performing units, Reuters reported, marking the co...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- EBay Inc. will eliminate 9% of its workforce in an effort to streamline operations and prioritize its best-performing units, Reuters reported, marking the company's second round of job cuts this year.

"As we work to capture the significant opportunity ahead, this step was taken to ensure we continue to operate from a position of strength by aligning our teams and resources with our top strategic priorities," an eBay spokesperson said in an emailed statement.

Shares of eBay initially plunged on the news before markets opened in New York, but recovered to little changed.

The latest reductions follow a round of job cuts in February, when eBay said it would eliminate around 800 jobs, amounting to 6% of its staff at the time. The company also enacted cuts in early 2023 and early 2024.

Earlier this year, eBay acquired secondhand fashion marketplace Depop, a deal that's expected to help eBay compete with Lithuanian upstart Vinted, which is expanding in the US. In August, eBay said the Depop deal was $200 million more than initially announced, which could weigh on earnings in the third quarter.

The company is set to report third-quarter financial results on Oct. 28.

articles.title: Musk backs SpaceX-Tesla merger idea as both boards form special committees
articles.summary: Elon Musk said on SpaceX's third quarter earnings call late Tuesday that he thinks merging the company with Tesla would be a good idea and revealed that both...
articles.body:
Elon Musk said on SpaceX's ( SPCX ) third quarter earnings call late Tuesday that he thinks merging the company with Tesla ( TSLA ) would be a good idea and revealed that both companies have formed special committees to study a deal.

Answering an analyst question on the call, the SpaceX and Tesla CEO took on the 800-pound gorilla in the room — a merger of his biggest companies.

"This is definitely kind of a question where I feel like I'm tap dancing through a minefield," Musk joked, before adding some new information.

"I think both SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees to discuss this idea," Musk said. "At the request of shareholders, and these special committees are consist of independent directors. And because I'm a conflicted party, I can't actually be in the discussions of the special committees."

SpaceX stock soared in premarket trading following the company's Q3 earnings release. But it was the merger speculation that garnered much attention.

Committees of independent directors are the standard structure when a controlling shareholder sits on both sides of a deal.

Despite the caveats, Musk said he thinks a tie-up would likely be a good thing.

"I don't think we should necessarily assume that I think some people out there assume that a SpaceX and Tesla merger is a certainty. And I think that would be overstating it. Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes," he said.

Last week, Barclays analyst Dan Levy said in a note to clients that a tie-up "has increasingly become the consensus expectation," Yahoo Finance reported .

Tesla must hold its annual general meeting (AGM) by Dec. 6, per SEC rules, and Barclays sees that as the appropriate avenue for shareholders to vote on a proposal.

Levy said a merger announcement that slips later into October or early November "may increasingly challenge merger approval as part of the AGM." In that case, a deal could instead come in the next six to 12 months, since investors see an advantage in closing under the Trump administration's friendly M&A environment.

Musk owns around 20% of Tesla, compared with about 48% of SpaceX, where supervoting Class B shares give him around 82% of the vote. SpaceX is worth about $2.1 trillion and Tesla about $1.5 trillion.

If SpaceX bought Tesla at those values, Musk would own about 37% of the combined company and control 56% of the vote, Levy said. That's well above the 25% Tesla stake he has long said he wants.

That's why Barclays expects SpaceX to be the buyer in an all-stock deal. At current values, each Tesla share would be worth about 0.7 SpaceX shares before any takeover premium.

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang: 'We have to accelerate AI safety'
articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says AI safety has to improve.
articles.body:
Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang says the AI industry needs to focus on safety following this summer's revelations that AI agents from leading labs broke free of containment and hacked into websites, including Hugging Face.

"It shouldn't have happened. Doesn't need to happen," Huang told Deirdre Bosa at Nvidia's GTC Berlin conference .

During his keynote on Wednesday, Huang revealed Nvidia's OpenShell Reference Architecture , which the company said will allow customers to build, contain, and observe AI agents. If an agent attempts to go rogue, Nvidia said the system can intervene and stop it.

"Hugging Face developed an exercise, a simulator, and they came to the conclusion: If OpenShell existed, their website wouldn't have been attacked that way," Huang said.

"We have to accelerate AI safety, and safety technology and capability to me is one and the same … As much as it is capable, you want it to be safe. The two of them are really one and the same. And so in the future, as we develop these AI capabilities, safety will come along with it," he added.

Part of that effort, the CEO said, comes down to establishing a zero-trust system around AI agents. Zero trust is a framework for protecting connected systems by limiting their exposure to other platforms and requiring people and platforms to regularly verify their identities.

Doing so, the thinking goes, reduces exposure to hacking and other cyberattacks.

"These agents are autonomous systems, and when you have an autonomous system on your computer … you should first start with zero trust, and give it minimum privileges, minimum access, minimum use of tools," Huang explained.

"Maybe they could access a file, but they can't delete the file. Maybe they can access the internet, but they can't … send stuff out," he added. "And so there are a lot of different things you could specify. Those practices about how to deploy agents and deploy autonomous systems [have] to be adopted across the board right away."

According to Huang, Nvidia is working with more than 100 companies to develop features to manage AI agents using OpenShell.

"We're working with all the labs and working with all the operating system companies. I think the [hacking incidents were] unfortunate, but I think that it's very much transformative for the industry," he added.

articles.title: Trump and allies float ideas for expanding Trump Accounts to adults
articles.summary: President Trump and allies have proposed making Trump Accounts, established as a saving vehicle for kids, accessible to adults.
articles.body:
President Trump and his allies have floated a series of ideas for another round of changes to Trump Accounts, potentially making them available to adults.

"We're looking at something as an alternative," Trump said on Tuesday when asked if the accounts could be expanded. He suggested there could be a parallel program "because it really is somewhat of a different thing, having to do with adults."

Brad Gerstner, CEO of Altimeter Capital and an early advocate of Trump Accounts, told the New York Post he was looking to expand Trump Accounts directly to make them accessible to anyone under 40.

He suggested Congress could take up the issue within months, an idea immediately picked up on Capitol Hill by Sen. Bernie Moreno, an Ohio Republican and Trump ally.

Moreno said he would lead the effort in the Senate and added that raising the age limit for the accounts would "give hardworking Americans powerful new tools to buy homes, wipe out student debt, and invest in their own futures."

Gerstner responded with a simple message: "DM me Bernie."

This lively back-and-forth comes as the shape of an expansion — or the prospects of passage if Democrats take control of either the US House or Senate in the coming elections — remains unclear. Still, many in Trump's orbit are emphasizing how central the accounts have become to the Trump administration's agenda and its final midterm message to voters.

Trump on Tuesday called the accounts "one of the most successful things people have seen ever in government."

Shifting rules and more high-dollar donors

The accounts were created last year as part of the Republicans' One Big Beautiful Bill Act to give parents a vehicle to save for their children.

The Treasury Department provided $1,000 in seed money for US citizens born between 2025 and 2028, invested in broad index funds.

Yet the Trump administration took a series of unilateral actions in recent weeks, including the auto-enrollment of more than 60 million additional children and the initiation of a plan allowing publicly traded companies to donate stock to accounts that would be held for at least five years.

Critics say that rule change could tie a child's long-term financial security to a single company rather than the broader economy, and they've raised ethical concerns that wealthy donors could use multibillion-dollar stock dumps into kids' portfolios to manipulate asset prices or secure tax write-offs.

Elon Musk this week became the highest-profile private donor, pledging to give one share of SpaceX (SPCX) stock to every child in America via the accounts.

articles.title: Russia to send first diesel shipment to US on Thursday amid global supply crunch
articles.summary: Russia will send its first 40,000-tonne diesel shipment to the United States on Thursday, under an agreement with President Donald Trump to resume Russian
articles.body: Russia will send its first 40,000-tonne diesel shipment to the United States on Thursday, under an agreement with President Donald Trump to resume Russian fuel supplies, Russia's deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said.The move comes as global diesel markets face a supply squeeze, while Ukraine has warned that renewed Russian energy exports could help finance Moscow's war effort.According to Reuters, Novak said further shipments would follow the agreement between Russian President Vladimir Putin and Trump, adding that Moscow would meet US demand within its capabilities. The first cargo is part of a broader supply plan announced by President Trump.Trump has announced plans for Russia to supply 300,000 metric tonnes of diesel initially, followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and another 1 million tonnes thereafter. The arrangement is aimed at increasing fuel supplies amid a global diesel shortage and rising prices.Russia had imposed a ban on diesel exports after Ukrainian drone strikes on its oil refineries disrupted production and caused fuel shortages in the country. On October 9, Moscow lifted the ban, allowing Russian suppliers to resume diesel shipments to international markets.The development comes after US President Donald Trump pushed for a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine targeting attacks on energy infrastructure. The proposed arrangement aimed to halt strikes on oil refineries, power facilities and other energy sites, as attacks on critical infrastructure disrupted fuel supplies and added pressure on energy markets.Ukraine has opposed easing restrictions on Russian energy exports, arguing that additional revenue from diesel sales could help Moscow finance its war effort.President Volodymyr Zelensky criticised the US-Russia arrangement, warning that allowing Russia to expand fuel exports while the war continues could weaken pressure on the Kremlin to end the conflict.Europe is also facing growing pressure on diesel supplies as disruptions to Middle Eastern exports tighten the market. Reuters reported in September that the disruption had cut Europe's diesel and jet fuel supplies by about a quarter, pushing fuel inventories to a 12-year low.Nigeria's Dangote refinery has increased exports to Europe to help fill the gap, highlighting the region's growing reliance on alternative suppliers.Reuters reported on October 21 that analysts expect the US-Russia diesel deal to have limited impact on global fuel prices, as the promised supplies may be too small to ease the market shortage. Analysts also questioned whether Russia could meet the announced export targets given damage to its refineries and rising shipping costs.With EU restrictions limiting direct imports of Russian fuel, the additional supplies are unlikely to provide an immediate solution to Europe's diesel concerns.You use AI every day. articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says data center builders have to be 'good neighbors'
articles.summary: Nvidia's Jensen Huang says AI data center builders have to be good neighbords.
articles.body:
Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang says that for data center builders to win over communities, they must first partner with them and be good neighbors.

"When you go into a community … before you start building, you ought to extend yourself out to the local community and partner with them," Huang told Deirdre Bosa during the company's GTC event in Berlin.

"Let them know what you're about to do is going to bring, of course, all the benefits, but it's going to, of course, bring new neighbors," he said.

Data center construction has faced major pushback across the US , with some counties and towns instituting outright bans on the facilities. New York has placed a one-year, statewide moratorium on data center construction. Texas, meanwhile, has put connecting new data centers to its grid on hold as it works to determine their potential impact.

The issue has even become a flash point in the midterm elections, with President Trump backing data center development, and Democrats and some Republicans campaigning against them.

Residents have lodged complaints about the constant noise generated by data centers, water usage, increased electricity costs, and more.

To help ease tensions with local residents, some companies, including Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Amazon ( AMZN ), have taken steps to win over municipalities by dropping controversial nondisclosure agreements (NDAs).

NDAs have become a key issue among some data center opponents, as they prevent local leaders from disclosing information about the projects.

"Everybody has now taken a step back, whether it's the NDAs or contributing to the communities, whether it's building shops and … community centers and improving schools and in many cases even supporting lower taxes and, you know, all kinds of benefits that can be brought to the local communities," Huang said.

"I think those are all good ideas, and each one of them ought to be … tailored for the needs of the community. But the most important thing is you've got to be a good visitor. You know you should be a good guest. And before you go into a community, stop by and see if you can be helpful," he added.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's core sector growth accelerated to 7.9 per cent in September 2026, up from 5.9 per cent in August, driven by strong output across six of the eight key infrastructure industries, according to data released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry on Wednesday.The Index of Eight Core Industries (ICI) tracks the performance of coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilisers, steel, cement and electricity. These industries account for 40.27 per cent of the weight of the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), making the index an important indicator of industrial activity.Iron ore production recorded the highest year-on-year growth at 18.4 per cent in September, followed by electricity at 11.4 per cent and coal at 10.7 per cent. Refinery products grew 10.3 per cent, cement output increased 9.8 per cent, while steel production rose 4.9 per cent during the month.In contrast, fertiliser production declined 11.7 per cent in September, while natural gas output contracted 4.6 per cent and crude oil production fell 1.4 per cent year-on-year.Coal, refinery products, steel and iron ore have been the major drivers of overall core sector growth in recent months, the ministry said.The cumulative growth rate of the core industries index stood at 5.1 per cent during April-September 2026, compared with 2.5 per cent in the corresponding period of the previous year, according to provisional data.The ministry also revised the final index for August 2026 upwards to 120.4 from the provisional estimate of 119.2. articles.title: Gonzalo Bernardos, economista, critica la falta de protección ante los desahucios: "Los hogares y las empresas no deberían asumir dicha protección social"
articles.standfirst: Gonzalo Bernardos critica la falta de vivienda pública en España tras el desahucio de Maricarmen
articles.summary: Gonzalo Bernardos critica la falta de vivienda pública en España tras el desahucio de Maricarmen
articles.body: El economista Gonzalo Bernardos ha criticado la escasez de vivienda pública en España y ha reclamado a las administraciones que asuman la protección de las personas más vulnerables ante situaciones como los desahucios. Lo ha hecho a través de una serie de publicaciones en X en las que denuncia la falta de recursos habitacionales y cuestiona la actuación de los responsables políticos. "Una sociedad civilizada debe proteger a los más débiles, especialmente a los menores de edad y a los ancianos, y disponer de las viviendas sociales necesarias para convertir un desahucio en un traslado", comienza Bernardos en su mensaje. El profesor de Economía considera que esta responsabilidad no debería recaer sobre los hogares ni las empresas, sino sobre las administraciones públicas, a las que los ciudadanos financian mediante sus impuestos. "Los hogares y las empresas no deberían estar obligados a asumir dicha protección social, pues ambos pagamos impuestos para que la haga la Administración", sostiene. En su crítica, Bernardos también apunta directamente a los responsables políticos. "No obstante, nuestros políticos incumplen el mandato que les hemos dado los ciudadanos", afirma antes de poner el foco en las cifras del parque público de viviendas. El economista utiliza los datos de 2025 para ilustrar la dimensión del problema. Según las cifras que recoge en sus publicaciones y en su artículo de opinión, España contaba ese año con 318.000 viviendas públicas, una cantidad que representaba el 1,2% del parque total de viviendas y el 1,6% del número de hogares. "En 2025, solo teníamos 318.000 pisos públicos, que únicamente suponían el 1,2% del parque total de viviendas del país y el 1,6 del número de hogares. Sin duda, una gran vergüenza", escribe. Las cifras forman parte del artículo que Bernardos ha publicado en su página web, titulado 'El caso Maricarmen: lo que no te han explicado'. En él analiza las circunstancias del desahucio de María del Carmen Abascal, conocida como Maricarmen, y reflexiona sobre el papel de las administraciones públicas en la protección de las personas con dificultades para acceder a una vivienda. La reflexión del economista parte de una idea central: disponer de un parque público de viviendas suficiente permitiría ofrecer una alternativa habitacional a quienes pierden su hogar y no cuentan con recursos para acceder a otro alojamiento. De esta manera, defiende que un desahucio no tenga por qué traducirse en una situación de desamparo. El pronunciamiento de Bernardos llega después de que el desahucio de María del Carmen Abascal, de 87 años, haya generado una fuerte repercusión social y política. La mujer fue desalojada el 23 de septiembre de la vivienda del distrito madrileño de Retiro en la que había residido durante décadas y trasladada posteriormente al hospital, donde falleció en octubre. Su caso reabrió el debate sobre la protección de los inquilinos vulnerables y la respuesta de las administraciones ante los lanzamientos. En su artículo, Bernardos también examina la historia del contrato de alquiler de Maricarmen, las condiciones de la denominada renta antigua y las circunstancias que desembocaron en el procedimiento judicial. Además, cuestiona la decisión de ejecutar el desahucio y sostiene que la existencia de alternativas públicas habría permitido abordar la situación de otra manera. El economista concluye que la protección de las personas vulnerables debe corresponder al Estado del bienestar y no depender exclusivamente de las decisiones particulares de propietarios o empresas. Su crítica vuelve así a situar la escasez de vivienda pública en el centro de un debate que ha adquirido especial relevancia tras el caso de Maricarmen.

articles.title: Booking, en el punto de mira de la UE: la investigan por las estafas que sufren quienes reservan en la plataforma
articles.standfirst: La Comisión Europea abre un expediente formal y cuestiona cómo protege los datos de los usuarios
articles.summary: La Comisión Europea abre un expediente formal y cuestiona cómo protege los datos de los usuarios
articles.body: La Comisión Europea ha puesto a Booking en el punto de mira. Bruselas ha abierto un expediente formal contra la plataforma de reservas por no tomar las medidas que le exige la Ley de Servicios Digitales (DSA) para frenar los anuncios fraudulentos y las estafas por suplantación de identidad, el conocido como ‘phishing’. Según el Ejecutivo comunitario, la compañía no ha “evaluado con diligencia ni mitigado de manera efectiva” los riesgos vinculados a este tipo de engaños. La investigación analizará si Booking ha aplicado medidas eficaces para reducirlos, como la retirada de anuncios fraudulentos. “La Ley de Servicios Digitales establece responsabilidades claras en las plataformas para abordar estos riesgos y debemos garantizar que la plataforma de reservas líder en Europa se tome en serio esas responsabilidades”, ha señalado la vicepresidenta de Soberanía Tecnológica, Seguridad y Democracia, Henna Virkkunen. Bruselas también cuestiona cómo protege la plataforma la información de clientes y alojamientos. Un portavoz de la Comisión ha expresado su preocupación porque Booking no esté protegiendo lo suficiente datos como los nombres, los números de teléfono y el correo electrónico de empresas y usuarios particulares. Además, la Comisión pone en duda que la compañía cumpla las normas de transparencia, ya que considera que no ha etiquetado con suficiente claridad como publicidad los anuncios de los alojamientos que pagan por aparecer en mejores posiciones en los resultados de búsqueda. El expediente no tiene un plazo fijado para su conclusión. Si finalmente se confirma el incumplimiento, la DSA permite imponer multas de hasta el 6% de la facturación mundial de la empresa. Las estafas que suplantan a hoteles o a la propia plataforma suelen seguir un patrón: mensajes urgentes que alertan de que la reserva se cancelará si no se confirman los datos de la tarjeta, a menudo con un enlace a una web falsa. Ante cualquier petición de pago que no coincida con la confirmación original, lo recomendable es no pinchar en el enlace y comprobarlo directamente en la aplicación oficial o con el servicio de atención al cliente.

articles.title: eMudhra shares plunge 20% after security flaw sparks global action
articles.summary: eMudhra shares fall 20% after weak TLS certificate keys trigger Mozilla, Google and Cloudflare revocations; CERT-In warns of website impersonation risk.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Following a 20% crash in eMudhra shares on Wednesday, a flaw in the generation of private keys linked to eight intermediate digital certificates has triggered a global security response, with Mozilla, Google and Cloudflare taking steps to prevent attackers from impersonating legitimate websites.The compromised keys could potentially allow attackers to create fake security certificates for websites they do not own, making fraudulent sites appear genuine to browsers and exposing users to the risk of intercepted or altered communications.The issue was reported on Oct 17 by Dennis Jackson, a member of Mozilla’s cryptography engineering team, who flagged weaknesses in the keys associated with the eight eMudhra intermediate certificates. The keys had been generated with insufficient randomness, making them vulnerable to recovery.In an update on Wednesday, eMudhra said a flaw during a key-generation ceremony on April 30 last year resulted in a second set of weak keys being generated alongside the original strong keys. The weak keys were subsequently published to browser root stores. The company is investigating the root cause.Private keys are secret digital codes used to sign security certificates. These certificates work like identity documents for websites, allowing browsers to check whether a site is genuine. If the keys used to sign certificates are weak or recoverable, attackers could potentially create fraudulent certificates and make fake websites appear trustworthy.The affected certificates were part of eMudhra’s global transport layer security (TLS) business. The certificates had also undergone independent audits for two consecutive years and had been included in browser trust lists since mid-2025.Mozilla blocked six affected website-security certificates in Firefox through OneCRL, its centralised list of revoked certificates. It also released security updates for Firefox desktop, Android and extended-support versions, and removed the relevant root certificate from its trust store.Google blocked the affected public keys through its Certificate Revocation List Set, while similar protection was rolled out to supported Android devices through Google Play services. Cloudflare has also introduced security measures across services that rely on certificate verification.Kaushik Srinivasan, co-founder of eMudhra, told TOI that the incident did not involve a breach of the company’s infrastructure or data, and that its Indian digital signature certificate (DSC), eSign and enterprise solutions businesses remained unaffected.Srinivasan told TOI that no certificates had been issued from the affected root in India and that there was only one customer in the US to whom the company had issued certificates under the affected infrastructure. The global TLS business accounts for about 1% of eMudhra’s revenue, he said.“In FY26, we reported revenue of about Rs 710 crore and EBITDA of roughly Rs 110 crore,” Srinivasan told TOI. The company had guided revenue growth of 15–18%, with a greater focus on enterprise solutions, which offer higher margins. Its overall strategy remains unchanged, he said. Srinivasan said the use of eSign in India continues to grow as the country digitises, particularly in banking, lending and e-governance. “We are part of that growth. However, those certificates and operations have nothing to do with the affected certificates in this incident.”While the direct business impact is limited, reputational risk remains a concern. Srinivasan told TOI that the company could not yet quantify the reputational damage and was working directly with customers to address concerns and help them transition to alternative providers where necessary.The flaw appears to have occurred during the key-generation process rather than through an intrusion into the company’s systems. The company is investigating the root cause and will consider an independent investigation if its internal review does not establish what happened. It will share its findings with relevant stakeholders and browser companies, he said.The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), in an advisory issued on Wednesday, warned that compromised keys could potentially be used to impersonate websites, intercept communications or issue fraudulent code-signing certificates that make malicious software appear to come from a trusted publisher. CERT-In has advised organisations to update browsers, applications and operating systems with the latest security patches.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Anthropic to publicly file for IPO as early as Friday, sources say
articles.summary: The move would mark a crucial next step for what could be the biggest IPO in history.
articles.body:
Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) is set to publicly file its S-1 investor prospectus as soon as Friday, according to three people familiar with the artificial intelligence firm's plans. The move would mark a crucial next step for what could be the biggest IPO in history.

The much-anticipated public debut , expected to surpass SpaceX's ( SPCX ) June IPO, is widely viewed as a crucial test of investor appetite for the artificial intelligence boom, as investors have become more concerned about the industry's massive spending.

Anthropic confidentially submitted a draft IPO registration statement to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) in June. Under SEC rules, companies using the confidential process must make their registration materials available 15 calendar days before the start of their formal investor roadshow.

Anthropic did not respond to a request for comment on the timing of its S-1.

A public filing would clear a key procedural hurdle toward a potential November listing, though the timing of the offering remains subject to market conditions and other factors. Crucially, it would also give regular investors their first look at the financial details and risks around one of the AI industry's fastest-growing companies.

Anthropic is spending billions on AI infrastructure to train and run its suite of Claude models. That includes working with Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) and Amazon ( AMZN ), as well as renting out graphics processor unit (GPU) capacity from SpaceX's Colossus 1 data center.

The company pulled in $16.3 billion in revenue over the first six months of 2026 and reported a net loss of over $80 billion, according to a Tuesday Wall Street Journal report . Wall Street is anticipating that the company could raise as much as $100 billion at a $2 trillion valuation, Reuters previously reported .

Last week, Anthropic told investors at its San Francisco office that its revenue climbed to $16.8 billion in the third quarter, up from $11.5 billion in the second quarter, according to the Financial Times , noting that the company is also profitable on an adjusted basis.

The colossal offering comes as this year's banner IPO market is becoming more challenging. Earlier this week, shares of South Korean data center provider Elice plummeted a staggering 32% during its first trading day after raising $151 million. Nvidia-backed Firmus Grid abruptly shelved plans for a public listing earlier this month after investors balked at its proposed valuation, while several other companies have postponed plans to go public, citing market conditions.

articles.title: eMudhra breach: IT ministry says digital signature & eSign services unaffected, sets up probe team
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has said that digital signature certificates and eSign services regulated by the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has said that digital signature certificates and eSign services regulated by the Controller of Certifying Authorities remain unaffected by the security incident involving eMudhra.The ministry said it had taken serious note of the incident and constituted a special team to investigate the matter. It also cautioned against social media accounts spreading fear about the incident's impact.The incident relates to the compromise of private keys associated with digital certificates issued by eMudhra, according to an advisory from the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), the government's cybersecurity watchdog.The IT Ministry said the reported security incident concerned eMudhra's global certificate business and that the impact on Indian websites was expected to be "very limited".Government sources said eMudhra operates separate Indian services, including eSign, and a global certificate business, adding that the issue arose in its global operations. "We are taking it up with them, and we are also taking it up with other operators to check whether they have further issues," a source said, as cited by PTI.In its advisory, CERT-In said eMudhra had reported a compromise of private keys associated with eight intermediate Certification Authority (CA) certificates in its public key infrastructure (PKI). These comprised six Transport Layer Security (TLS) certificates and two code-signing certificates.Digital certificates establish trust in online assets, while TLS protocols help secure data transmission between browsers, applications and websites. Private and public keys are used in encryption and other security processes to protect digital communications.CERT-In warned that the compromised keys could be exploited by cybercriminals to issue fraudulent certificates for domains they do not control. Such TLS certificates could be used to impersonate legitimate websites and facilitate man-in-the-middle (MitM) attacks, potentially allowing attackers to intercept or modify encrypted communications. The compromised code-signing keys could also be used to issue fraudulent code-signing certificates.eMudhra said the incident had no connection with its Indian Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) and eSign businesses and affected only a small part of its global TLS business. The company added that its infrastructure had not been compromised, no data had been breached, and its physical and logical security controls remained intact.According to eMudhra, a flaw in its system led to the creation of weak keys alongside the original strong keys. A researcher had alerted Apple, Google, Microsoft and Mozilla that the weak keys could potentially be reverse-engineered using AI-assisted techniques.The company said its affected global TLS business accounted for around 1 per cent of its revenue, although the incident could pose reputational risks that could not be quantified."eMudhra is working directly with customers who may be affected to give them replacement certificates, so that critical services are not disrupted. The company is also working with the root programs and continues its root-cause investigation," eMudhra said.CERT-In said Google had blocked the public keys of the affected TLS intermediate certificates in Chrome through a Certificate Revocation List Set (CRLSet) update. Google has also announced the removal of eMudhra's emSign ECC Root CA-G3 from the Chrome Root Store. The change is scheduled to be rolled out to all devices relying on the Chrome Root Store on October 27, 2026.Mozilla has also blocked the six affected TLS intermediate certificates issued by eMudhra.Founded in 2008, eMudhra is a Bengaluru-based digital trust and cybersecurity company headquartered at Hi-Tech Defence and Aerospace Park in Jala Hobli, Karnataka.It provides digital trust and cybersecurity solutions for businesses, including Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), digital signatures, SSL/TLS certificates, identity and access management, multi-factor authentication, document signing and digital workflow platforms.The incident comes as the State Bank of India (SBI) disclosed the suspected exposure of 3,897 customer records containing personally identifiable information on the dark web. The bank reportedly received alerts about the suspected exposure from its threat intelligence service provider on October 16.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Iran war impact: Indian Oil plans to reduce Middle East crude purchases under annual deals in FY28
articles.summary: Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), India's largest refiner, plans to scale back crude oil purchases from Middle Eastern suppliers under annual contracts for
articles.body: Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), India's largest refiner, plans to scale back crude oil purchases from Middle Eastern suppliers under annual contracts for the financial year 2027-28, as the prolonged Iran war continues to disrupt shipments and push up transportation costs.The state-run refiner is expected to make a modest reduction in its annual contracted volumes from Gulf producers, Reuters reported, citing a source familiar with the matter.The move marks a shift in IOC's procurement strategy, with Indian refiners traditionally sourcing more than half of their crude requirements from the Middle East. The region has remained a preferred supplier because of its proximity to India and availability of heavier, high-sulphur crude grades.For the current financial year ending March 2027, IOC had planned to source around 47 per cent of its crude imports from Middle Eastern producers through annual agreements on a free-on-board (FOB) basis, under which the buyer bears shipping costs after the oil is loaded.However, disruptions linked to the Iran war, now in its eighth month, have complicated these arrangements. Attacks on vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial shipping route for Gulf oil exports, have restricted tanker availability and pushed freight rates close to record highs.The supply uncertainty has forced several Asian refiners to suspend purchases under some existing annual contracts and increasingly turn to the spot market to secure alternative supplies.Some oil producers have responded by offering crude on a delivered basis, taking on part of the increased freight costs to remain competitive.Despite the disruptions, IOC and other Indian refiners have recently purchased Iraqi crude at discounts to the Dubai benchmark under FOB arrangements, according to the Reuters report.Indian refiners had initially increased imports of Russian crude to offset the shortfall in Middle Eastern supplies. However, Russian oil purchases could moderate in the coming months if shipments through the Strait of Hormuz improve and Gulf producers offer more competitive prices and freight terms to retain their share of the Indian market.Meanwhile, the shipping crisis has also affected IOC's plans to expand its vessel capacity. In July, the company floated a tender to acquire stakes in at least two very large gas carriers but has since put the award process on hold.The cost of a 10-year-old vessel has nearly doubled to around $150 million since the tender was issued, making the proposed investment significantly more expensive.The concerns come as global crude prices remain elevated amid fresh threats to Middle Eastern energy shipments. Brent crude futures climbed 1.23 per cent to $110.10 per barrel on Wednesday, while US West Texas Intermediate crude rose 1.21 per cent to $99, according to a Times of India report. articles.title: Russia to send first diesel tanker to the US amid Trump deal
articles.summary: Russia will send on Thursday its first diesel tanker to the US to an undisclosed port.
articles.body:
Russia will send its first tanker of diesel fuel to the United States on Thursday, Russia’s Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak told reporters amid a deal with US President Donald Trump.

The vessel will have 40,000 tonnes of fuel, but Novak, who made his remarks on Wednesday, did not name which US port the fuel would be delivered to.

Russia lifted its ban on diesel exports on October 9, which Moscow originally put in place to tackle the country’s shortages as Ukrainian-led drone strikes hindered production capacity.

The shipment comes despite setbacks for Russia’s diesel output. Earlier this month, Ukraine’s Ministry of Defence said that drone strikes knocked out at least half of Russia’s oil refining capacity, forcing cuts at Russia’s top diesel-producing refineries.

“Additional shipments will follow, of course. There were agreements reached between the two leaders. We will meet the United States’ needs, to the extent of our capabilities,” the RIA Novosti news agency quoted Novak as saying.

That was echoed by US special envoy Steve Witkoff, who has been meeting Russian President Vladimir Putin for talks in St Petersburg.

“We are preparing deliveries of several vessels, the tankers, right now. They will go one after another. The financial component should be provided,” he said, adding that Russia would also be able to supply fertilisers in “large quantities” to the US market.

US President Donald Trump had previously said that Moscow would export 300,000 tonnes, or 2.25 million barrels, followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and 1 million tonnes “immediately thereafter”.

US consumers have continued to face high prices at the petrol station, particularly for diesel fuel, a pressing point as the country heads into midterm elections in less than two weeks. The average price for a gallon of diesel is $6.31 ($1.70 per litre), according to the American Automobile Association (AAA). While prices remain well over the $6 mark, they are on the downturn. The average price a month ago was $6.51.

articles.title: Canada wants to expand its LNG business. Critics raise red flags
articles.summary: As Canada’s LNG exports grow, critics raise concerns over human rights abuses linked to major corporate investors.
articles.body:
Kitimat, British Columbia: As Canada tries to position itself as an emerging leader in global liquefied natural gas (LNG) markets, it risks locking in multidecade, multibillion-dollar contracts with companies whose current and past ventures include human rights abuses and environmental damage.

LNG Canada, which began operations in mid-2025 in Kitimat in British Columbia on the country's west coast, is the nation's first major export facility.

In late September, it gave the green light to a $33bn expansion which will double production in the coming years at Kitimat.

But the Kitimat plant has had challenges with its flaring equipment since beginning commissioning in late 2024. In 2025, the new liquefaction facility burned 350 million cubic metres of gas due to an issue with its main flare stack.

“The flaring noise was on a whole other level when they were first getting started up,” a resident who asked not to be named said in an interview. “It was just huge, way bigger than I think it was supposed to be.”

“I am devastated about the changes to my home territory,” another resident said. “I can't always see the stars like I used to from my parents' place here. My friend returned temporarily, and her asthma has been much worse.”

The residents requested to remain unnamed because Kitimat is a small community and the industrial project is a major employer and donor to local organisations.

The project has political support, especially as Canada faces economic pressures from United States President Donald Trump’s administration, which has unleashed a slew of tariffs on it, including on Canadian steel, lumber and aluminium in 2025 and added an additional suite of tariffs on Canadian products worth $20bn in August, including wine, dairy and textiles.

Since Trump started his tariff campaign, the Canadian government has announced a flurry of deals and agreements aimed at diversifying trade partners and expanding domestic infrastructure developments.

articles.title: AI helped find a critical security flaw affecting 70% of the internet
articles.summary: Researchers at three different companies said Wednesday that they used AI to discover and address a set of critical bugs that could affect 70% of the internet.
articles.body: Researchers at three different companies said Wednesday that they used AI to discover and address a set of critical bugs that could affect 70% of the internet. The vulnerabilities were uncovered by teams at OpenAI, Google-owned cybersecurity company Wiz, and another cybersecurity company, Calif. The bugs, collectively called PHP2Shell, could allow attackers to execute code and read memory that could contain sensitive information, like passwords. AI played a crucial role in Wednesday’s discovery, allowing researchers to conduct cybersecurity work across multiple apps in just hours, the companies said. The disclosure comes after advancements in AI have raised concerns from Washington to Silicon Valley about how the technology could supercharge cyberattacks. “With frontier AI models and the right tools, a single researcher completed in a week what previously would have taken a world-class team months of work,” Wiz researchers wrote in a blog post on Wednesday. Researchers at Wiz used Google’s Gemini 4 Argon, Wiz Atlas and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol during the research process. The bugs were discovered in late August but were disclosed to the public on Wednesday after PHP had a fix for it. The PHP Foundation, the organization behind the coding language PHP that is at the center of the vulnerability, has released a patch for the bugs and is urging website operators to update their systems immediately. The flaws could allow attackers to remotely execute code, disrupt services and expose customer data, according to web infrastructure provider Cloudflare, which has been working with the PHP Foundation, Calif, OpenAI and Wiz to address the issue. The National Security Agency in a social media post urged organizations using PHP to update their systems, or take them offline if they’re unable to do so. The disclosure prompted some government websites in Europe to go offline as companies updated their systems, according to Reuters. Wiz researchers say the issue is on par with the Heartbleed bug from 2014, which impacted an encryption technology estimated to be used by two-thirds of the Web. Heartbleed allowed cybercriminals to access that data that should have been protected. Like Heartbleed, the researchers at Wiz say PHP2Shell could similarly serve as a turning point in cybersecurity. While the vulnerabilities existed for years, AI made it practical to deploy them. “The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve,” Wiz researchers wrote in a blog post. “Frontier AI models substantially reduced that barrier, turning a longstanding flaw into an exploit.”

articles.title: Buffett's Berkshire just trounced chip stocks and flashed a rare dot-com-era signal
articles.summary: Investors traded chip stocks for shares in Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway, sending them to an intraday record and opening the widest gap with chips sinc...
articles.body:
For three weeks, Wall Street sold the hottest trade in the market and bought one of the oldest. Chip stocks lost 15% while Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway gained 7%.

That swing carried Berkshire's Class B stock ( BRK-B ) to a record close Tuesday, its first since May 2, 2025 — the day before Buffett said he would hand the CEO job to Greg Abel. The stock pushed to an intraday record Wednesday, as did the Class A stock ( BRK-A ).

The wait took 17 months, a stretch in which the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) gained more than 35%.

From Oct. 6 through Tuesday, the iShares Semiconductor ETF ( SOXX ) fell in 10 of 11 sessions. Berkshire rose on nine of those days, and on chips' two worst days, Oct. 14 and Oct. 16, it posted two of its best gains of the run.

For now, that price action has made Berkshire look like a hedge against the AI chip trade. Since Oct. 1, it has mostly risen on the days chips fell.

Berkshire is on track to rise in 14 of its last 15 sessions. Along the way, it strung together a 10-day winning streak, its first since 2018, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.

From Oct. 2 through Tuesday, Berkshire beat SOXX by 22 percentage points. That's the widest gap over any 12-session stretch since early 2010, according to Yahoo Finance calculations that compare Berkshire with the PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) back to 1994. The 12-session window is the one that captures this month's widest gap.

Chips fell at least 14% while Berkshire gained at least 7% over 12 sessions. Before this month, that last happened Oct. 3, 2001. Every earlier case came in 1995-96 or in 2000-01, the latter as the dot-com bubble burst.

History sends a mixed message from here.

In the near term, chips bounced. They were higher a week later in five of the six earlier cases, and they're rebounding Wednesday,too. A year out, chips were lower in five of six instances, and the S&P 500 fell in four.

Four of those six cases came during the same bear market, though. Treat this as a rare signal, not a forecast.

Abel has also changed how Berkshire uses its cash. Berkshire bought back about $4.5 billion of its own stock in the second quarter and ended 14 straight quarters of net stock selling while its cash pile fell from a record $397 billion.

Buffett said Sept. 18 he would also step down as chairman. The stock bottomed two weeks later.

The next test comes with third quarter results, expected to be released Saturday, Nov. 7.

articles.title: Mortgage demand is falling off a cliff, even as rates stabilize
articles.summary: Mortgage applications are continuing to fall, even as rates hover around 7.4%.
articles.body:
Mortgage applications have continued their downward slide even as mortgage rates ticked down for the first time in months.

Applications for new home purchases dropped 7% through Friday compared to a week earlier, while refinancing deals were down 2%, according to Mortgage Bankers Association data. Compared to a year ago, purchase applications are down 18% as buyers remain priced out of the market.

The latest declines come even as the average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage dropped for the first time in two months to 7.41%, according to MBA calculations, suggesting that many buyers feel priced out by current market conditions.

"It is very clear that the higher mortgage rate environment has cooled the housing market this fall," Joel Kan, the MBA's vice president and deputy chief economist, said in a statement.

National Association of Realtors data released on Tuesday showed that pending home sales plunged in September to the lowest level in 25 years.

Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.
